**The Liberal media is questioning my loyalty!

_They are questioning where my allegiance lies after I sacrificed both my legs and nearly my life in service to the United States of America._**
I served in the U.S. Army for more than 12 years. I lost both of my legs on the battlefield fighting terrorists in Afghanistan. I then learned how to walk again and continued fighting for freedom in the halls of Congress. I also volunteered alongside the Israeli Defense Forces. So, if someone thinks that my showing support for our ally Israel is a display of anything other than absolute patriotism and American loyalty, **[they are dead wrong.](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=1c8c0416945f46a4a8bf8a8a3627a5a0&_e=ypTuR-tfsWbJB0oAB9apVKim_zHDNarGpG0RXDDjgLnYHoNptk9x4nod6afIXpQ5qn3gFGJQGDBPJv7gJHaGM4g15zFxnbZSswrV9---j3PsXSSrzVFYvcH0J2iMTEchc2RhDIRasJLuZUFBLuPqeFuz_OXGJX6eX9N3XnwJOahIz2gkPGDwYHGVT8fKHtaqVAnOZd3EFeTAoWyu5ao5MDZdRP9tZlx7iElgoUqAo0N5VdpMGNLvypkYcPLp5U6k-dMv3kbsciOng113-uND4Qukucd8hwBTU6Djjcs_lsI5fb3x5a_NF5OyM_34P2m_FSHreiEI9vypoAU_8wObygXK7cD80QWnZ9SNBonV0CIoCaju8c8-LWVb5cj2dg-tYJCCl1f5i18jTtGc1AT4bw%3D%3D)**

**They can call me heartless, soulless, or anything else they want, but if they think they know more than I do about the impacts of radical Islamic terrorism, they’re flat-out delusional.** Every day I wake up and look where my legs used to be is a vivid reminder of exactly what’s at stake in the fight against terrorism.

Clearly, though, they are not going to stop coming after me or questioning my loyalty — **the loyalty of a double-amputee Purple Heart veteran with more than 12 years of American military service!** The Radical Left truly is a [disgrace](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=1c8c0416945f46a4a8bf8a8a3627a5a0&_e=ypTuR-tfsWbJB0oAB9apVKim_zHDNarGpG0RXDDjgLnYHoNptk9x4nod6afIXpQ5qn3gFGJQGDBPJv7gJHaGM4g15zFxnbZSswrV9---j3PsXSSrzVFYvcH0J2iMTEchc2RhDIRasJLuZUFBLuPqeFuz_OXGJX6eX9N3XnwJOahIz2gkPGDwYHGVT8fKHtaqCAMc519QWfwMeJlf9EVwylURDnR5cBJ8IfKEyWLYCmFbtudfKI22vtmhP_AVZRr_Stp7XpIRqeyVhSpE8_WsKPdbFl-IKMquMnJnORyU6Qh-9bYgdCpQ4azOc_ZrIXRyV1qhuL7ZeR7hiyLAvC0v8G-P43oYxCDcyedxemArPHiZ6v8_B_YkKv-bL5LMWOcr) in our great nation.

Peter,

_Do you have a few minutes?_

I wanted to take a moment and personally share my story with a true patriot like you.

This is Greg Abbott here, Governor of the great state of Texas.

I was born in Wichita Falls, Texas, and was raised in Duncanville. Growing up, I was involved in various activities, including baseball, Boy Scouts, and track and field.
[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=f092beea44394d5289a8c8889970e5fe&_e=zS2KYP837iPeo_EOdh_LDBPBxlC7LuU14pLqO3tfO3iHMpOMeAR58k0uAdtaaojW5N2Yyzax3rNVJQsQbHwzcOiHumCm_QbZEIJUInNkCBu9y_Tkc6Qj_5hTl4Zj3DmTFg-Y5wOrXZXIjSLqzROzq2poj9RDuzdu749jA9w_CDs-iTIunGhh15RB98-pIKDNYoHZY-g4pM3EqRK4VohXZtQXPsUY2sfvQQx8N1o-O2H4cFFLD4KW6yWmwOlin4Jsvgh4aZo-MvMwSqkckNczJHIMBa9gBMCGFWodNmqOBQT0c5irB-Rhw1bDYy14WqB7zysUg2qBpwKdPMD1F-tjC6j2-x1TDweSXUubOEmZEIU8z5cdVSPjf_M9xRRPj5sObPvJBm0HbzOlqAx9GWNifQ%3D%3D)
Education has always been very important to me, so I decided to further my education after high school. I went on to attend the University of Texas at Austin and graduated with a B.B.A. in finance. Later on, I earned a law degree from Vanderbilt University.

In 1981, I proposed to the love of my life, Cecilia, on the San Antonio Riverwalk, and we got married later that year. It was the best decision I've ever made!
[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=f092beea44394d5289a8c8889970e5fe&_e=zS2KYP837iPeo_EOdh_LDBPBxlC7LuU14pLqO3tfO3iHMpOMeAR58k0uAdtaaojW5N2Yyzax3rNVJQsQbHwzcOiHumCm_QbZEIJUInNkCBu9y_Tkc6Qj_5hTl4Zj3DmTFg-Y5wOrXZXIjSLqzROzq2poj9RDuzdu749jA9w_CDs-iTIunGhh15RB98-pIKDNYoHZY-g4pM3EqRK4VohXZtQXPsUY2sfvQQx8N1o-O2H4cFFLD4KW6yWmwOlin4JsIwu0B6PcM7EeikHV7fASxwCob2fDqZSAGJhF6-N6NClSZ1258TNsbYCuPylZ7fuvAniH6ojuxu3JLgU43iy8NrSQb1JSZCDaM_BmLbb-h53A_60v9Wij3cBhSVYexOqFhTClDK-lGaRVTjeJvLqa4A%3D%3D)
Peter, everything changed in 1984. One day while I was out jogging, a tree fell on me and left me partially paralyzed. From that moment on, I knew my life would never be the same.
[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=f092beea44394d5289a8c8889970e5fe&_e=zS2KYP837iPeo_EOdh_LDBPBxlC7LuU14pLqO3tfO3iHMpOMeAR58k0uAdtaaojW5N2Yyzax3rNVJQsQbHwzcOiHumCm_QbZEIJUInNkCBu9y_Tkc6Qj_5hTl4Zj3DmTFg-Y5wOrXZXIjSLqzROzq2poj9RDuzdu749jA9w_CDs-iTIunGhh15RB98-pIKDNYoHZY-g4pM3EqRK4VohXZtQXPsUY2sfvQQx8N1o-O2H4cFFLD4KW6yWmwOlin4JsP8AfuelM9l3v2yn2-Z1yK1b_yG2dhjZ579v8poBsLXw5s5yLRIIU69ZNxBW02uZWf34GBRGlrNGQcf3CGB8tiq-cl0-KSKn4FNFBjbZ0RMBtdiRmVm33z3a30EEKsm2Z62eHFVZK1oZh2E_tcafzhg%3D%3D)
From my faith and my family, I gained strength during this difficult time. I learned to recognize that our lives are not defined by our challenges but by how we respond to them. _And I chose not to let this accident break my spirit._

Instead, I turned to the Scripture passage _James 1:12_ , which got me through the most difficult season of my life. I had faith in God and trusted in his plan for me.
_**" Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him."
\- James 1:12**_
_Peter, during challenging moments in our lives, it 's important to remember what matters the most to us_. For me, it's my faith, my beautiful wife Cecilia, my amazing daughter Audrey, and of course, our three dogs, Peaches, Pancake, and Honey Butter Chicken Biscuit!
[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=f092beea44394d5289a8c8889970e5fe&_e=zS2KYP837iPeo_EOdh_LDBPBxlC7LuU14pLqO3tfO3iHMpOMeAR58k0uAdtaaojW5N2Yyzax3rNVJQsQbHwzcOiHumCm_QbZEIJUInNkCBu9y_Tkc6Qj_5hTl4Zj3DmTFg-Y5wOrXZXIjSLqzROzq2poj9RDuzdu749jA9w_CDs-iTIunGhh15RB98-pIKDNYoHZY-g4pM3EqRK4VohXZtQXPsUY2sfvQQx8N1o-O2H4cFFLD4KW6yWmwOlin4Js15L4a7Br0YDz56PG52D3qAraV3eFbBM2t-SNOZoV3cpIuH5b32uNKDqOkO93SL1wJnEUK5W2KB9pcqqN0zyE5OB7EsWMDr82oDwYipERjnmEaKxgNed9wfPS713S7ReiGdGknf59extA8eWaO7QOYg%3D%3D)
I often say our lives are not defined by the obstacles we encounter but our response to those challenges. _This rings true for our state and its people, too. _

Under Joe Biden's administration, Texas and all of America face unprecedented challenges daily.
_**[Our southern border is overrun with dangerous criminals.

I’m reaching out to you today not just as a former president, but as a fellow citizen who’s deeply invested in our country’s future. When I think back to the day Joe was elected president, I remember feeling a profound sense of hope, pride, and a great amount of relief. clean_body: I need you to read this. It’s time for Joe Biden and Democrats like Jacky Rosen to face accountability. Will you STAND WITH ME today? | | | After winning the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate in Nevada and President Trump's endorsement, I have a simple message for the American people. America, I've got you. Please remember these three words: \- Accountability \- Leadership \- Hope America is not in the same place we were four years ago. Our country has been under assault from within and without. The crisis on the border was totally created by Joe Biden. It has led to the deaths of so many Americans from fentanyl and opioid overdoses. He has allowed hundreds of known members of terror watch lists to come across our border. Joe Biden has taken over 80 executive actions to weaken our sovereignty, to weaken our national security, to allow our border to become the crisis that it is. And Jacky Rosen has done NOTHING to push back. When we talk about accountability we talk about why this economy isn't working for everyone. Why are prices so high? Why have we abandoned American energy independence, American energy security? Why does this administration and Jacky Rosen put politics over people? The issues abound. And what Joe Biden and Jacky Rosen have done is they've left a wake of hardship and destruction on so many Americans. It's about leadership that will take seriously serving the people. It's about leadership that will secure our borders. It's about leadership that will go after the cartels. It's about leadership that will honor our sovereignty. It's about leadership that will pursue American energy security. It's about leadership that will lower taxes. It's about leadership that won't use issues and regulators to hold individuals and businesses hostage. It's about leadership that will make sure we have Constitutional judges instead of activist judges. It's about leadership that prioritizes families and parents and their kids' education over the bureaucracy that is ruining it. Because it does us no good to ACKNOWLEDGE the challenges that we've all been dealing with, it does us no good to TALK about what leadership could be because hope is a fragile thing. I know that firsthand. And I've talked to so many Nevadans and so many Americans who are at a point like I was in 2008, when we were THIS CLOSE to allowing hope to be extinguished. But I tell you what, the beautiful miracle of that day came from the voice of my gunner as I was laying there in the dirt and the dust of that Kandahar battlefield. Having just given up the will to live, he came up to me, having been wounded himself, under fire, and he said “Sir, I've got you.” Those words still give me chills today. When I got blown up in Afghanistan in 2008, I shouldn't have lived that day. And yet, when I surrendered to my Creator, when I surrendered my soul, when I surrendered my life, that's when I found the ultimate purpose. I've been blessed to live the American Dream. I ask for no man, no woman's pity. I don't ask for sympathy. I don't ask for acknowledgement of the service I've already done. I have had a beautiful life. I have an incredible, supportive wife. We've been married for 15 years and we're blessed with three incredible children. I've realized the American Dream. It allowed me to be a business owner. I've realized the American Dream when I've had a roof over my head and food on the table and gas in my car. It's time to deliver hope because the American Dream is NOT dead. The American Dream is not dead because the American Nightmare of Joe Biden and Jacky Rosen begins to end RIGHT NOW. We're not fighting for my campaign for Senate, we're fighting OUR campaign for Nevada. We don't fight for my political movement, we fight for OUR grassroots movement. And we look forward not to my election, but to OUR election. We look forward to our election where we will deliver to DC, where we deliver for the people, and where we give to all Americans and all Nevadans who desperately need it. ## **Michael Cloud Just Voted to Defund NATO**
---
Hi Peter, Our extremist Congressman, Michael Cloud, just voted to defund NATO.Cloud was one of 46 Republicans who supported a new bill aimed at defunding NATO, our alliance established over 75 years ago to keep America and its allies safe.NATO, or the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, was established under American leadership to unite our allies in North America and Europe, with the purpose of deterring the military aggressions that led to the World Wars. NATO was key to our victory in the Cold War and the preservation of democracy in Western Europe.Cloud, in backing this measure, seems to have overlooked the invaluable lessons of history – lessons that were paid for dearly by those who made ultimate sacrifices on the beaches of Normandy 80 years ago.The potential ramifications of defunding NATO are grave: it would render America less secure and more susceptible to potential threats.Cloud's decision doesn’t save money, but increases the burden on the US by reducing the allies we have to share costs with. Worse, it jeopardizes the security of all Americans.If this news troubles you as much as it does me, join me in taking action to vote Michael Cloud out of office and elect a first grade teacher who remembers the most important lessons from history.

This district represents a critical opportunity to take back the House and oust our Congressman who’s shown time and again that he’s out of touch with the needs of Virginia voters.
He opposed access to birth control and protecting abortion access. He voted to overturn the 2020 election. He opposed veterans getting healthcare after exposure to burn pits. And he voted against capping the cost of insulin. **He had his chance and failed — that much is clear.**
And this November, we’re going to do something about it. I’m incredibly proud of the movement we’ve built, and can’t wait to see what the **#Mehta-Verse** does in the months to come.
We’ve got a lot to do, Peter, so let’s get to work!

subject: Bodily Autonomy Is On The Ballot
body:
We need more pro-choice voices in Congress. | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/9053805b5841/reproductive-rights-are-on-the-ballot-12697762?e=5d7e9a146c)
---
|
# Reproductive rights are on the ballot.

Because of the Trump administration, women’s rights and reproductive freedom has been under attack. We can’t undo the overturning of Roe v. Wade, but we can elect more pro-choice leaders to the House of Representatives.
As the proud father to two wonderful daughters, and an even prouder grandpa to one fiery little girl, it infuriates me that Geneva, Nicole, and Kate all have less rights to their bodies now than anytime before, because extremist state governments and overzealous prosecutors criminalize abortion and miscarriages.

_**And they aren’t just stopping with abortion — the Republican Party has given us their playbook.**_

We know they’re coming after IVF and birth control. Nothing is safe. This election is critical for so many reasons, one being the futures for our daughters and granddaughters.
My opponent, Russell Fry, supports a national abortion ban. He voted to ban abortion while he was in the South Carolina House of Representatives and he’s voted to ban abortion since joining the United States House of Representatives.
**
We can restore reproductive rights, but only if we remove extremists like Russell Fry from Congress.**
[Join my campaign](https://malhyman.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=98998055a4d4c8cdda41af3ea&id=bc3611a906&e=5d7e9a146c) and let’s fight for all the women and girls who deserve full control over their bodies and their futures.
---
| 📸 : 2022 Reproductive Rights Rally in Myrtle Beach, SC

Please see a special message from our

Dear
Fellow American,

My name
is Larry P. Arnn, and I'm the president of Hillsdale College, a
Christian liberal arts college in southern Michigan. Hillsdale
was founded in 1844 with the mission of providing "sound
learning" of the kind needed to preserve "the blessings of civil
and religious liberty."

A few
years ago, members of the world's elite met at the annual World
Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, and launched the Great
Reset initiative.

What is
their plan, and what does it mean for America?

In short,
they aim to transform the world economy. As Klaus Schwab-the
founder and executive director of the Forum-wrote, "We need a
'Great Reset' of capitalism." If successful, their plan would
also have the effect of destroying our American way of life.

This
initiative is not merely about economic reform. It is an attempt
to impose global rule by so-called experts.

Some
social media companies are censoring our efforts to promote a
seminar we hosted on the Hillsdale campus that explored the topic
of the Great Reset. Fortunately, we can communicate directly with
you.

In this
seminar, we consider the idea of the Great Reset and its
implications for America. But that's not all. We also delve into
pro-freedom alternatives to this tyrannical plan.

Sign up

**Good Morning**! On this day in 1910, the first Father's Day was celebrated in Spokane, Washington, created by [Sonora Smart Dodd](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxsz7FugzAQANCvsbcg3_liYPDQhS1dOyKDz-FagyOwQPn7Sp37A096X4_xESTL9vwMK_uayhjmKieP7gb9DWkkHX1iRraaPbTQdQZbC3rx0RChm2bnYIow9aaz4W4imzmGtktJi0eDZBz0pkcgaCwEZkuWYUptIqvIcJRa9ua7yFYXTvldTt6buaw6-6XW16Hsh8JB4XBdV7PIUcv-zrL9NGV_KhwGyaxw6One6d3H1yU5y-FaRea5Bsl_VP0_dnr8DQAA__8s-k-N) and local ministers. By the 1920s, it was celebrated nationwide and became an official U.S. holiday in 1972. After Monday's win, the Boston Celtics now boast an impressive 18 championships, the most in NBA history. What's even _more_ remarkable is that [Bill Russell](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxsz81K7DAUAOCnSXZTcn5uO1lkcUGKguNOXJakPWkjmcnYppV5e8G1L_DB93EZLj7ldJvf_FVcjWXwY02HDO0J7Al5YD25KIJCWhx0cD4b7Aj04mxkjj6MgYB5RD929swMyBb_tbY1Ojk0yKYFaywCQ0PgRYhJIMQuMik2MqVa1uazpFtdJOZHOWRtxnLV2S213jdF_xX2CvtH2eveBFHYf83PQK_h5T3Mivoovu6rKHraFr_KpFc33b9TzmlrO8VmvvqUf8n6d_Bw-BMAAP__D4RRXw) was part of 11 of those teams. You can watch his best highlights [here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxsz81K7DAUAOCnSXZTcn5uO1lkcUGKguNOXJakPWkjmcnYppV5e8G1L_DB93EZLj7ldJvf_FVcjWXwY02HDO0J7Al5YD25KIJCWhx0cD4b7Aj04mxkjj6MgYB5RD929swMyBb_tbY1Ojk0yKYFaywCQ0PgRYhJIMQuMik2MqVa1uazpFtdJOZHOWRtxnLV2S213jdF_xX2CvtH2eveBFHYf83PQK_h5T3Mivoovu6rKHraFr_KpFc33b9TzmlrO8VmvvqUf8n6d_Bw-BMAAP__D4RRXw). ## Dual Wildfires Spread in New Mexico
As California battles wildfires that started over the weekend, New Mexico faces two fast-moving fires on the Mescalero Apache Reservation, near the village of Ruidoso. [See video and photos here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskL1y3SAUhJ8GdWjggMVVQZGGzmlTajA6WCfmRwNcKX77jJ027c7u7Hzfr9ft1VOi8v7TZ7Qj1s2HQRduC5crB73pabcREVBNaKWRj4cAo-R0WC3DKmTUUhv1BlHsIaBfzQv6xbxoBRNZEKDFIlexgtRyVtIjKq1QvkUTtWJa4E6jtvl3pTIOjOmzXtjmUPOU7DHG2Zn6wcAxcPd9z5hO3-ugjP2rw8D1UdsnA1fw7gzc1yEDJxYGTj7-5TzjHwqV35T2SA159icfzYcPbLw9aa-98pI5Xj48_aBaeK_PcfBY2wf_XnSfBg-1DE8lYxkMnNFSqWXVQhgGbmp2P29KifpimBbv2VP6xhj_l3pZ-BsAAP__-Hl5Xg). As of Tuesday afternoon, both New Mexico fires remained 0% contained. [The South Fork Fire](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxs0L1u7CAUBOCnwR0WHJB_CorbuNvbprQwHNYni40DrK28feTU6UbfNKP5eMwPS5H253-7oakhzdZVOnHuuBw56Fk33gREQNWgkb0cBgG9ks1qZFiEGpwaFuxAi8V7CdqOrvfOLx3ohgwI0KKToxhBatkqaRGVViiX0AetmBboqabcfiba64ohfqcTc-vS1kSz1noUpv4xmBhM13W1r_yFd8lg2vEqt1L0gTLeuaR3XXlI-cVv4vlNPpXENyzORsyJ28O6FXnGgvm0ldLOYGqy8cdFMVLpeqbFc7MUfyfUvw85DfwEAAD__7-mZUg) had burned approximately 15,000 acres near Ruidoso, affecting an estimated 500 buildings. Authorities urged the 7,800 residents to evacuate, writing on social media, "GO NOW. Do not attempt to gather belongings or protect your home." The second fire, dubbed [the Salt Fire](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxs0LFu9CAQBOCnwR0WLMjgguJv3N3fprQwLOdNsHEwspW3jy5VinSj-YqR5u0xPzxl2p___YaupTL70OjCeeBy5KBn3UWXEAFVh04aaa0Ao2S3OqHMYkX0yxg0KCusxWCNHpIJwYdh6ciBAC0GOYoRpJa9kh5RaYVySSZpxbTASK3U_r3Q3lZM-atcWPtQti67tbXjZOofg4nBdN93_1E_8YUMph3v89VSjokq_s684lFqw8jLzjc8g89YC_eHD-sLT6yXb1R2BlNXXTxuypnOwTAtnpun_LPf_n7jcvAdAAD__2wjZAg), covered an additional 5,500 acres. The Mescalero Apache Tribe is also receiving reports of multiple additional fires on the reservation.
## Senate Probes Boeing's Safety Scandals

## Baseball Legend Willie Mays Dies at 93
Willie Mays, one of the greatest baseball players of all time and arguably the [greatest center fielder ever](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLGO6yAQAL8Gd1jLQoxdULyGLq-90sJmSfaE7QhQLP_96VJfO9OM5us-3wNn3h__w0aupWMOa-M3zYNUk0Qzmy66RISkO3LKqnEEtFp1T3dTkGClMIVkETAtw5JgHOwypTjYhTp2CGhgUBNMqIzqtQpE2mhSS7LJaGGAIrej9N8H7-1JKV_Hm0q_HluX3bO1VxX6n0Av0J_n2VN97b9SoN_yItDXdpRLoJ8Feo4CvQE94s2AQJ_pQXsM5ZIr7Y2KTEw5UpEn58wkt3BVGZmqnHRXXHx9eB2sMPDYAudPRvt7ytvhTwAAAP__Nkpjiw), died Tuesday afternoon. The "Say Hey Kid" was 93. Mays played from 1951 to 1973, most of it with the Giants, first in New York and then in San Francisco when the team moved west in 1958. He was the National League home run champion four times and finished his career with 660 home runs and 3,283 hits. I want to reach out to introduce myself today and tell you a bit about why my race in California is a must win if we’re going to take back the House from MAGA extremists and hold the line against Donald Trump. 1. I represent a seat in California’s Central Valley which has been named one of the most competitive in the country. Democrats recently added me to their Frontline list of most vulnerable members because we desperately need more resources to keep this seat blue.

2. I’m one of Donald Trump and Mike Johnson’s top targets this year. They’ve announced $2 million in TV reservations in our media market, and GOP SuperPACs are already spreading disinformation to our latino communities.

3. My opponent this year has been called the GOP’s “Dream Candidate” to run against me. He’s the Mayor of Stockton, the biggest city in the district, and he’s on the record saying he’ll vote against women’s reproductive rights.

4. A terrifying new poll shows us down by 4 points. If that’s the case, there is no way Democrats will take back the Speaker’s gavel. We have to make sure these aren’t the results we see on Election Day.

5. The end-of-quarter deadline is coming up and we need your help to have a strong showing. We can’t afford to be outraised by our Republican opponent, who is getting a huge boost from Trump’s guilty verdict.

This initiative is not merely about economic reform. It is an attempt to impose global rule by so-called experts.

Some social media companies are censoring our efforts to promote a seminar we hosted on the Hillsdale campus that explored the topic of the Great Reset. Fortunately, we can communicate directly with you.

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 6/19/2024
body:
Your daily rundown of REAL news for REAL Coloradans.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
This is the Mountain Minute for Wednesday, June 19, 2024.
- Heidi Ganahl
---
|
---
| | **TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
---
**[Report finds more Colorado 4th-graders struggle with reading, 8th-graders with math, than those who don't](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE CENTER STAGE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Colorado's fourth-grade students are struggling to read and its eighth graders are having trouble with math, according to this year's [KIDS COUNT Data Book](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) published by The Annie E. Casey Foundation.

The [report](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) stated 62% of fourth graders weren't proficient in reading in 2022. In 2019, the year before the COVID-19 pandemic, 60% of fourth graders weren't proficient. Nationally, 68% of all fourth graders aren't proficient in reading, compared to 66% in 2019.

Eighth graders not proficient in math [increased to 72%](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in 2022, an increase in nine percentage points since 2019. The national percentage for the category is 74%, an increase of seven percentage points since 2019.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Why is Democrat Adam Frisch running TV ads in 3rd District primary? To boost his chances in November](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Adam Frisch is running TV ads in Colorado's 3rd Congressional District GOP primary, spending $100,000 to challenge Jeff Hurd and [shape the primary outcome](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Frisch aims to sway GOP primary voters towards Ron Hanks, a candidate he perceives as easier to defeat in the general election due to Hanks' controversial stances.
* The ads [criticize Hurd](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for avoiding debates and not disclosing his presidential votes, painting him as the beneficiary of corporate super PACs.
* Frisch's strategy could inadvertently [strengthen his opposition](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), potentially leading to a harder campaign against a more formidable Republican nominee.
* Significant spending and involvement from [national groups and super PACs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) are influencing the primary, with both sides using media aggressively to support their preferred candidates.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Shooting of man standing at door not covered under'Make My Day' immunity, Colorado Supreme Court rules](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The Colorado Supreme Court ruled that a Denver man, Joseph M. Howell, cannot claim ['Make My Day' immunity](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for shooting a man outside his apartment because the incident occurred on a concrete slab, not inside a dwelling.
* Howell shot a man acting threateningly from inside his ground-floor apartment through a closed security door, aiming at the man who was on the concrete pad outside. Howell argued that the concrete pad should be considered part of his dwelling for purposes of 'Make My Day' immunity, which permits [lethal force against intruders](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) inside a dwelling.
* The court maintained that the concrete pad does not qualify as a dwelling because it lacks walls and a roof, thus not meeting the [law's definition](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) of a structure capable of containing people.
* Howell remains liable for prosecution without immunity, as the court stressed that the protective scope of the 'Make My Day' law is strictly confined to the [interior of a home](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[10.5% of ballots have been cast in primary election statewide; 12.7% in 4th District](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* In [Colorado's 4th District](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), 12.7% of registered voters have already voted in the primary, with 34.1% of these being unaffiliated voters.
* Douglas County shows the [highest ballots cast](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in the district, contributing significantly to the total ballots cast. Larimer and Weld counties also have notable returned ballots.
* Statewide, about [10.5% of Colorado's registered voters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) have participated, with older age groups showing stronger participation rates. Gender differences in voting patterns are evident, with more females voting Democrat and more males voting Republican.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Biden to take sweeping election-year action shielding estimated 550,000 from deportation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [POLITICO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* President Joe Biden announced a [new immigration policy](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to shield approximately 550,000 undocumented spouses and children of U.S. citizens from deportation.
* This initiative, named "[parole in place](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)," extends a policy previously applicable to military families, and is part of Biden's broader immigration strategy that combines restrictive and protective measures.
* The announcement aligns with the [12th anniversary of DACA](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), aiming to bolster Biden's support among Latino voters and address criticisms from his base over recent restrictive border policies.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Ranchers press CWD officials for answers in daylong summit on wolves](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Ranchers and state officials, including Colorado Parks and Wildlife (CPW), met at a summit in North Park to discuss impacts of [wolf reintroduction](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on livestock, expressing deep concerns over current and future wolf populations.
* The summit, held at Gittleson Ranch which has experienced significant livestock losses due to wolves, highlighted [ineffective non-lethal control methods](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and the urgent need for better management strategies.
* Discussions focused on [rebuilding trust](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) between ranchers and CPW, enhancing communication, and addressing the socioeconomic effects of wolf predation on local communities.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

Casey Foundation. The stated 62% of fourth graders weren't proficient in reading in 2022. In 2019, the year before the COVID-19 pandemic, 60% of fourth graders weren't proficient. Nationally, 68% of all fourth graders aren't proficient in reading, compared to 66% in 2019. Eighth graders not proficient in math in 2022, an increase in nine percentage points since 2019. The national percentage for the category is 74%, an increase of seven percentage points since 2019. | Adam Frisch is running TV ads in Colorado's 3rd Congressional District GOP primary, spending $100,000 to challenge Jeff Hurd and . Frisch aims to sway GOP primary voters towards Ron Hanks, a candidate he perceives as easier to defeat in the general election due to Hanks' controversial stances. The ads for avoiding debates and not disclosing his presidential votes, painting him as the beneficiary of corporate super PACs. Frisch's strategy could inadvertently , potentially leading to a harder campaign against a more formidable Republican nominee. Significant spending and involvement from are influencing the primary, with both sides using media aggressively to support their preferred candidates. | The Colorado Supreme Court ruled that a Denver man, Joseph M. Howell, cannot claim for shooting a man outside his apartment because the incident occurred on a concrete slab, not inside a dwelling. Howell shot a man acting threateningly from inside his ground-floor apartment through a closed security door, aiming at the man who was on the concrete pad outside. Howell argued that the concrete pad should be considered part of his dwelling for purposes of 'Make My Day' immunity, which permits inside a dwelling. The court maintained that the concrete pad does not qualify as a dwelling because it lacks walls and a roof, thus not meeting the of a structure capable of containing people. Howell remains liable for prosecution without immunity, as the court stressed that the protective scope of the 'Make My Day' law is strictly confined to the . | In , 12.7% of registered voters have already voted in the primary, with 34.1% of these being unaffiliated voters. Gender differences in voting patterns are evident, with more females voting Democrat and more males voting Republican. | President Joe Biden announced a to shield approximately 550,000 undocumented spouses and children of U.S. citizens from deportation. This initiative, named "," extends a policy previously applicable to military families, and is part of Biden's broader immigration strategy that combines restrictive and protective measures. The announcement aligns with the , aiming to bolster Biden's support among Latino voters and address criticisms from his base over recent restrictive border policies. | Ranchers and state officials, including Colorado Parks and Wildlife (CPW), met at a summit in North Park to discuss impacts of on livestock, expressing deep concerns over current and future wolf populations. The summit, held at Gittleson Ranch which has experienced significant livestock losses due to wolves, highlighted and the urgent need for better management strategies. | | Friends, Happy Juneteenth. On this day, 159 years ago, the last enslaved people in Galveston Bay, Texas, learned they were free. Since then, June 19 has become a day to celebrate the Black experience in our country with community gatherings and reflections on the journey towards equality. In the years that followed emancipation and Reconstruction, Jim Crow era laws stripped away rights and freedoms from Black Americans. We’ve seen this pattern before in our country, where we have moments of incredible movement forwards, and then we face a powerful backlash, and violence rains down on the Black community. Tactics like poll taxes, literacy tests, and violent intimidation made it harder for Black Americans to vote and be a part of our democracy. To this day, we’re still seeing bigoted lawmakers place hurdles between Black voters and the ballot box, because they’re afraid they’d lose their power once Black Americans are able to fully use theirs. We encourage you to honor this day by:
* Checking the status of your voter registration
* Supporting your local leaders who are championing voting rights
* Talk with your friends and family about their plan to vote in November

Friend,

I can't tell you how much it means to me that you opened this. Did you know that only about 20-30% of folks open these messages from me?

I do have to ask a quick favor of you - I'm simply asking you to read this all the way through. If you finish reading this and you still think a $1 donation doesn't matter, then I want to just say **[thank you for hearing me out.](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z0n38k2n3hmo51q1d1rtpouo9k6dismh80g0r9gg_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs)**

While only about 25% of our friends are opening messages from me and my team, **[only about 1%](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zcql0rr612epibr4js67fqam87i483a9bqg5v77o_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs)** will go the extra mile by donating! I'm not exaggerating when I say this, Friend, conservatives like me rely on emails, texts, mail, and phone calls to stay in touch with supporters like you.

I don't have deep-pocketed billionaires that I can call on to hit these goals. **[I rely on the couple of bucks that hard-working Americans receiving these messages can afford to give me from time to time.](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z1uhf87stspvbqtm6nrjen996u7hci1740e274tg_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs)**

If everyone reading this chipped in just a little bit - even just $1 - we would be able to reach our goals and keep up with the Democrats' _MASSIVE_ campaign coffers.

**[I'll be honest...](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zi39235c2r6a8n84vegsi868b2nuausnfmjo6pho_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs) **

The Democrats were able to stop our Red Wave in 2022, and we need every little bit of support we can get if we want to fund the programs needed to win in 2024 - and we need it today. If we're going to stay on pace to reach all of our goals, I truly need your help.

[](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zcoj468nal8deq3otp552rvdpe2nsrt170haqsk8_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs)

**[I know it's not much, but all I need from you today is the price of a single cup of coffee, a candy bar, or a jelly doughnut. The Democrats rely on billionaire megadonors who give thousands at a time, but I rely on folks like you who can give $3, $9, or even $18.25 to reach my next crucial Goal.](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z8jo47fp1oqa1sfeur37fq7ue3b21veaiff2fa38_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs)**

**[☕CHIP IN THE PRICE OF A CUP OF COFFEE☕](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z4lq5jet6fbegaoa8c9lbosbn7cir4ef5f060m4o_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs)**

_Democrats are hoping I give up on you.

They're hoping you give up on me.

They're hoping both of us give up on conservative values altogether. _

We can't let them run this country into the ground. I'm rolling up my sleeves and continuing to work for hard-working families like yours - making our country better, stronger, and safer.

I hope you won't quit on me or our shared values. I know a lot of folks are going to ignore this, but I **[need](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zu1orlk2e3kvjuou8m8oml39mpf2qkq791gbn5q8_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs)** patriots like you to see what's at stake. If you think you're better off than you were 5 years ago, then I understand why you don't want to donate today.

**[But if you think we need to get this country back on track and restore the American Dream, please donate whatever you can afford before midnight.](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zs5c003msr1ff436567pmpqqk1gv5v2r88oih308_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs)**

**[DONATE TODAY](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z4avfd2cmdl715de63iunun5sjer11gck7h1ph7g_rp22sh2s8i6ep30s3i6cpr2c1h2bs)**

Juneteenth is more than a historical commemoration, it's a call to action
Today's holiday has been celebrated by Black communities for over 150 years and its recent federal recognition marks a milestone of American equity and progress.
https://www.votedrbob.com/post/juneteenth-is-more-than-a-historical-commemoration-it-s-a-call-to-action [https://www.votedrbob.com/post/juneteenth-is-more-than-a-historical-commemoration-it-s-a-call-to-action]
On this day in 1865, Union soldiers arrived in Texas with news that the Civil War had ended and slaves were now free.
Juneteenth is a day that deserves recognition from every American because true freedom cannot exist until it is granted to every last one of us.
LEARN MORE [https://www.votedrbob.com/post/juneteenth-is-more-than-a-historical-commemoration-it-s-a-call-to-action]
This holiday commemorates not just emancipation but the day when the good news reached everyone. It serves as a reminder that freedom delayed is justice denied and true liberty is only achieved when it is extended to all.
On top of generations of barbaric injustice, slaves in Galveston were cheated of their freedom for two years, highlighting the importance of the government championing secure liberty not for some, not for most, but for all.
Today, our work is not over. Creating a more just society is a perpetually unfinished task, and our fight for equality is eternal.
Juneteenth also serves as a call to action. We must challenge and improve the systemic structures that perpetuate racial oppression in every corner of the country.
We must strive to eliminate the remnants of racism that still exist today — because injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.
Happy Juneteenth, friends.
Happy Freedom Day.
-Bob

logo [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP61/1/113591/images/Kleinmann_Interim_Deliverables_Email%20Banner.png]
Hi Peter,
More than two years after President Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation, word finally reached Texas. On June 19, 1865, Union soldiers announced the proclamation in Texas. Juneteenth is our remembrance of that date.
This Juneteenth, I’m reflecting on the rich anti-slavery tradition in Kansas. All along the Kansas-Missouri border, slavery abolitionists fought in the 1850s and 1860s to end an unspeakable practice. The Free State is their legacy.
A happy Juneteenth to you and your family!
Matt

Today is Juneteenth and I wanted to take the opportunity to elevate an iconic Civil War story that they just don't teach in schools. To be sure, you absolutely should use today as an opportunity to follow amazing Black writers and content creators like [Dara Starr Tucker](https://substack.com/redirect/d891ce6c-2eff-4262-aec9-7d87d85b5465?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Khalil Greene](https://substack.com/redirect/ab507724-4a65-4780-b083-ce2a7c1e333f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Ijeoma Oluo](https://substack.com/redirect/dda94e98-e8e9-47f8-9789-6dd8ad66eb65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Conscious Lee](https://substack.com/redirect/c3252b2a-2bf2-421e-bb77-d7c2c2ef1120?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Ashani Mfuko](https://substack.com/redirect/8c881610-ff5b-42af-8f63-fd002577d90d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Ernest Crim](https://substack.com/redirect/06d95cde-6ac8-413b-add4-54057e903649?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and many many more. And here's [an excellent piece on Juneteenth by Michael Harriot](https://substack.com/redirect/dbc5bd37-9acb-4838-b48f-6242b301cbb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
For my part, today I want to share the Civil War story of Private Mohammed Kahn, also known as John Ammahail. At a time of rising anti-Black violence, anti-immigrant policy, and anti-Muslim hate, Kahn's story pushes back against such division and discord, and instead exemplifies the beauty of what this country can be.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2550223&post_id=145676674&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQ1Njc2Njc0LCJpYXQiOjE3MTg4MDIzNTMsImV4cCI6MTcyMTM5NDM1MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTI1NTAyMjMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.Eeu9tjn9auAFkBwuPFrR3sKU0bJFiZF__Q35FzKxlDY)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fe29cf4a-c0bf-4544-9380-c048472f1c84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Image of Mohammed Kahn's pension paperwork. Credit: National Archives
Private Kahn was one of only 250 Muslim soldiers who fought in the Civil War. His story is even more unique, however, as he fought in the famous Battle of Gettysburg, is believed to be one of only two Muslim soldiers who received a pension, and may be the only Muslim soldier who was also an immigrant.
Born in Persia, modern day Iran, in or around 1830, Mohammed Kahn was raised in modern day Afghanistan. He immigrated to the United States in 1861, during the period of antebellum America. Also known as John Ammahail, Kahn quickly made friends upon arrival. The Civil War broke out in April of 1861. Only two months after his arrival, and after a night out with his friends, Mohammed Kahn became Private Mohammed Kahn when he enlisted in the 43rd New York Infantry Regiment. The 43rd New York Infantry Regiment was an all white unit. Kahn was a person of color, yet evidently passed as "white enough."
This is where his story truly begins and becomes history.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..0D4gZwZK5AmG67uWpSHpJq0Z7k0pnl4FV8TiKRo7mKQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=145676674)
Khan spent the first two years of the Civil War as a cook serving the Union Army. That all changed in July of 1863 when Private Kahn fought in the infamous Battle of Gettysburg. Mere days after the battle and perhaps due to the ensuing chaos, he was separated from his unit. As he was not white, the Union guards who found him arrested him in Hagerstown, Maryland, and brought him before the Provost Marshall's headquarters to explain himself.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/92a1f5f2-e0f1-410b-a4ed-722f253595fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Battle of Gettysburg (1863), lithograph by Currier & Ives. Credit: Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. (LC-USZC4-2088)
Despite his best efforts, and perhaps due to his limited proficiency in English, Kahn was unable to convince the Union Army that he himself was in fact part of the Union Army, and part of the all white New York's 43rd Infantry. Because he was of color, and described as having dark complexion, and even though he had just fought in one of American history's most famous battles to end the scourge of slavery and white supremacy in America, they believed he could not be part of the white unit, and held him under military arrest.
As punishment, Kahn was sent to Philadelphia and put to work with recently escaped enslaved people. He spent months and months trying to find anyone who could vouch for him, reunite him with his New York 43rd, or even a member of the New York 43rd--but to no avail.
All that changed 10 months later in May of 1864. The Battle of the Wilderness was set to begin in Fredericksburg, VA between General Grant's Union Army and General Lee's Confederate Rebellion Army. Private Kahn, having learned that the 14th New York Infantry was taking a train down to partake in that battle, devised a remarkable plan. In his time in what was effectively a slave labor camp, Kahn had befriended an enslaved person, and conceived the plan with his support. His friend was tasked with distracting the prison guard, while Kahn prepared his escape. Kahn waited patiently and timed his escape with the departing train, and took off on foot.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..0D4gZwZK5AmG67uWpSHpJq0Z7k0pnl4FV8TiKRo7mKQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=145676674)
Running as fast as he could, Kahn chased after the train and jumped on to it at the last possible moment as it pulled out of Philadelphia station. By the time the prison guard realized what happened, it was too late. Kahn was already out of their grasp and on a train headed back into battle. As Kahn hoped, he found and remained with the 14th New York Infantry on this trip, that is, until Washington DC. From here, he traveled nearly 70 miles by foot down to Spotsylvania, Virginia by following other squadrons.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/78cde7c9-1934-4def-853b-d92260ce74d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Battle of the Wilderness marked the first stage of a major Union offensive toward the Confederate capital of Richmond. Credit: History.com Getty Images
Private Kahn arrived on May 7, 1864, on the last day of the Battle of the Wilderness and remarkably found and was reunited with his 43rd infantry unit. Joining his brothers once more, Kahn reengaged his service and fight to help the Union Army win. Only 15 minutes into the battle he was wounded with a gunshot to his left hand.
Kahn, an immigrant who arrived in the United States just months before the Civil War broke out, had now served as a cook, fought in the Battle of Gettysburg, suffered 10 months in a prison camp, escaped and found a miraculous way to reunite with his Unit, fought in another battle, and suffered a major injury. But far from using this injury as an excuse to exit the War, and he certainly would have been justified, Kahn persisted.
Undeterred, he refused to leave the war, and took the time to heal. And after his hand healed, Private Kahn returned once more to the field of battle, this time as a sharpshooter, and served through almost the entire Civil War until it ended the following year in April of 1865.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..0D4gZwZK5AmG67uWpSHpJq0Z7k0pnl4FV8TiKRo7mKQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=145676674)
Private Kahn's pension application records in detail the battles in which he fought, the injuries he suffered, and the duties he performed both as a cook and as a soldier. Private Mohammed Kahn died on May 26, 1891 in Manhattan, New York. He was buried at Cypress Hills National Cemetery in Brooklyn, Kings County. His burial plot is 2, 5009. Pictured here is his gravestone.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/94f5acd5-9e41-4f78-a8f0-c1a194b72fff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Private Mohammed Khan's gravestone at Cypress Hills National Cemetery in Brooklyn, Kings County
I first learned about Mohammed Kahn while researching for an opinion editorial on the vast contributions of Muslim Americans to our nation's history. Contrary to the popular perception that Muslims or Islam are new to America, Muslims have thrived in America since before America even existed, and have fought to defend this nation in every battle since the Revolutionary War, and to expand national participation in democracy. As [Michael Harriot remarks](https://substack.com/redirect/115ab7e2-938f-44a5-b2b9-65b32b12d62b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> I think that is what Juneteenth means to me and to a lot of people. I also think that it is just as important as the 4th of July, or more important, because this is the first time that America took a real step toward democracy. That's when the majority of this country were able to participate in democracy.
Mohammed Kahn's story is about that power of perseverance to overcome obstacles, the power of good to conquer hate, and the power of justice to conquer injustice. And while this article is a heavily summarized story of his life, remarkably, there are no books on Private Mohammed Kahn. Meanwhile, his full and complete 209 page pension is preserved in the [US Government National Archives](https://substack.com/redirect/df6c11dd-ccf0-4b77-a3de-22f17bb57a29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Given the opportunity, perhaps I'll take the initiative to write this much needed book about a critical and precious story of American history.
For now, I hope you found value in this inspiring story of Private Mohammed Kahn, a hero of the American Civil War.

An iconic untold story of an immigrant Muslim American in Antebellum America | | | Jun 19 | | | | | | | | | | | | Today is Juneteenth and I wanted to take the opportunity to elevate an iconic Civil War story that they just don't teach in schools. To be sure, you absolutely should use today as an opportunity to follow amazing Black writers and content creators like , , , , , , and many many more. And here's . For my part, today I want to share the Civil War story of Private Mohammed Kahn, also known as John Ammahail. At a time of rising anti-Black violence, anti-immigrant policy, and anti-Muslim hate, Kahn's story pushes back against such division and discord, and instead exemplifies the beauty of what this country can be. | | ---|---|--- Image of Mohammed Kahn's pension paperwork. Credit: National Archives Private Kahn was one of only 250 Muslim soldiers who fought in the Civil War. His story is even more unique, however, as he fought in the famous Battle of Gettysburg, is believed to be one of only two Muslim soldiers who received a pension, and may be the only Muslim soldier who was also an immigrant. Born in Persia, modern day Iran, in or around 1830, Mohammed Kahn was raised in modern day Afghanistan. He immigrated to the United States in 1861, during the period of antebellum America. Also known as John Ammahail, Kahn quickly made friends upon arrival. The Civil War broke out in April of 1861. Only two months after his arrival, and after a night out with his friends, Mohammed Kahn became Private Mohammed Kahn when he enlisted in the 43rd New York Infantry Regiment. The 43rd New York Infantry Regiment was an all white unit. Kahn was a person of color, yet evidently passed as "white enough." This is where his story truly begins and becomes history. Khan spent the first two years of the Civil War as a cook serving the Union Army. That all changed in July of 1863 when Private Kahn fought in the infamous Battle of Gettysburg. Mere days after the battle and perhaps due to the ensuing chaos, he was separated from his unit. As he was not white, the Union guards who found him arrested him in Hagerstown, Maryland, and brought him before the Provost Marshall's headquarters to explain himself. | | ---|---|--- The Battle of Gettysburg (1863), lithograph by Currier & Ives. Credit: Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. (LC-USZC4-2088) Despite his best efforts, and perhaps due to his limited proficiency in English, Kahn was unable to convince the Union Army that he himself was in fact part of the Union Army, and part of the all white New York's 43rd Infantry. Because he was of color, and described as having dark complexion, and even though he had just fought in one of American history's most famous battles to end the scourge of slavery and white supremacy in America, they believed he could not be part of the white unit, and held him under military arrest. As punishment, Kahn was sent to Philadelphia and put to work with recently escaped enslaved people. He spent months and months trying to find anyone who could vouch for him, reunite him with his New York 43rd, or even a member of the New York 43rd--but to no avail. All that changed 10 months later in May of 1864. The Battle of the Wilderness was set to begin in Fredericksburg, VA between General Grant's Union Army and General Lee's Confederate Rebellion Army. Private Kahn, having learned that the 14th New York Infantry was taking a train down to partake in that battle, devised a remarkable plan. In his time in what was effectively a slave labor camp, Kahn had befriended an enslaved person, and conceived the plan with his support. His friend was tasked with distracting the prison guard, while Kahn prepared his escape. Kahn waited patiently and timed his escape with the departing train, and took off on foot. Running as fast as he could, Kahn chased after the train and jumped on to it at the last possible moment as it pulled out of Philadelphia station. By the time the prison guard realized what happened, it was too late. Kahn was already out of their grasp and on a train headed back into battle. As Kahn hoped, he found and remained with the 14th New York Infantry on this trip, that is, until Washington DC. From here, he traveled nearly 70 miles by foot down to Spotsylvania, Virginia by following other squadrons. | | ---|---|--- The Battle of the Wilderness marked the first stage of a major Union offensive toward the Confederate capital of Richmond. Credit: History.com Getty Images Private Kahn arrived on May 7, 1864, on the last day of the Battle of the Wilderness and remarkably found and was reunited with his 43rd infantry unit. Joining his brothers once more, Kahn reengaged his service and fight to help the Union Army win. Only 15 minutes into the battle he was wounded with a gunshot to his left hand. Kahn, an immigrant who arrived in the United States just months before the Civil War broke out, had now served as a cook, fought in the Battle of Gettysburg, suffered 10 months in a prison camp, escaped and found a miraculous way to reunite with his Unit, fought in another battle, and suffered a major injury. But far from using this injury as an excuse to exit the War, and he certainly would have been justified, Kahn persisted. Undeterred, he refused to leave the war, and took the time to heal. And after his hand healed, Private Kahn returned once more to the field of battle, this time as a sharpshooter, and served through almost the entire Civil War until it ended the following year in April of 1865. Private Kahn's pension application records in detail the battles in which he fought, the injuries he suffered, and the duties he performed both as a cook and as a soldier. Private Mohammed Kahn died on May 26, 1891 in Manhattan, New York. He was buried at Cypress Hills National Cemetery in Brooklyn, Kings County. His burial plot is 2, 5009. Pictured here is his gravestone. | | ---|---|--- Private Mohammed Khan's gravestone at Cypress Hills National Cemetery in Brooklyn, Kings County I first learned about Mohammed Kahn while researching for an opinion editorial on the vast contributions of Muslim Americans to our nation's history. Contrary to the popular perception that Muslims or Islam are new to America, Muslims have thrived in America since before America even existed, and have fought to defend this nation in every battle since the Revolutionary War, and to expand national participation in democracy. As : I think that is what Juneteenth means to me and to a lot of people. I also think that it is just as important as the 4th of July, or more important, because this is the first time that America took a real step toward democracy. That's when the majority of this country were able to participate in democracy. Mohammed Kahn's story is about that power of perseverance to overcome obstacles, the power of good to conquer hate, and the power of justice to conquer injustice. And while this article is a heavily summarized story of his life, remarkably, there are no books on Private Mohammed Kahn. Meanwhile, his full and complete 209 page pension is preserved in the . Given the opportunity, perhaps I'll take the initiative to write this much needed book about a critical and precious story of American history. For now, I hope you found value in this inspiring story of Private Mohammed Kahn, a hero of the American Civil War. The Constitution established a limited
government in which the people ruled through their elected
officials. Under this form of government, America became the
freest and most prosperous nation in history.

system is one that increasingly exists in name only.

citizens.

Peter,
It’s Juneteenth — marking 159 years since freedom finally reached enslaved Black Americans in Galveston, Texas. And today, while we celebrate the end of slavery, we must do all we can to remember those who endured the unconscionable, this nation’s original sin.
You’ve heard me, and others, say this a lot, but we have to say it again: The march towards true, lived freedom is far from over. The struggle continues to this day, but the victories we’ve achieved are only because of the commitment of every new generation to engage in the fight for justice and equality.
And don’t get me wrong, we have come a long way since that day 159 years ago in Galveston, Texas. We have made our country a more welcoming, safe, and equitable place for Black Americans. **But there is still a long road left to travel.**
This Juneteenth, while we recognize the continued struggle, I’m still filled with hope for what’s ahead. Our power to make change has never been stronger. All voices in our democracy deserve to be heard, and I’m proud to be working alongside you in the fight to make that a reality.
Together, let’s use today to recommit to our shared effort to have this nation live up to its founding ideals.
Thank you for being in this movement, and happy Freedom Day.
Eric H. Holder, Jr.
82nd Attorney General of the United States

subject: This Juneteenth is a reminder
body:
Hi Friend, Today, I am reminded about the history we mark on Juneteenth. On June 19, 1865, people still held in bondage in Galveston, Texas, finally learned that slavery had been legally abolished and that they were free. | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87179174/480306601/-1283252511?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzU1YjYzNmMtM2QyZS1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=JhtXd-Mo3tZGnzpvScCt0FfLW4hBd2W4iwQE3EhLohU=&emci=b599f487-342e-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=755b636c-3d2e-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=12466492)
---
| | Hi Friend,
---
Today, I am reminded about the history we mark on Juneteenth.
---
On June 19, 1865, people still held in bondage in Galveston, Texas, finally learned that slavery had been legally abolished and that they were free.
---
Juneteenth is also a reminder of the tireless work of Black Americans, abolitionists, and generations of activists who have made it their mission to ensure America’s founding principles are truly secured for all Americans.
---
Black Americans were an integral part of our nation’s founding. You know, America’s first Black military unit — the First Rhode Island Regiment — came together in a multiracial coalition to fight for our independence and turned around the fortunes of the Revolutionary Army.
---

name: Josh Gottheimer
subject: Proud to commemorate Juneteenth
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOSH GOTTHEIMER FOR CONGRESS
body:
# [#] On June 19, 1865, the last enslaved Black Americans were informed of their freedom in Galveston, Texas – a full two years after the passage of the Emancipation Proclamation.

Juneteenth not only serves as a day to celebrate the countless achievements of the black community across our nation but also as a reminder that the arc of history does not bend toward justice. We must bend it. Together, we should recommit to those principles of justice and equality. We all know that there is more work to do. By acknowledging that, we begin the important task of recommitting ourselves to building a future that is more inclusive and supportive for all.

New Jersey began recognizing Juneteenth as a state holiday in 2020, a leader in the nation. Three years ago, Congress established Juneteenth as a federal holiday, and I’m proud to have cast my vote in favor of recognizing this important day.

But, we can’t forget that it shouldn’t have taken this long in the first place — and the long wait is only a sign that the struggle for equality is not over. There is still much more work to do.
We must recommit ourselves to taking action together. The road ahead will not be easy, but I know that, in the greatest country in the world, our best days will always be ahead.

This Juneteenth, let’s reflect on our past, and keep fighting for equality and justice!

Yours,

Josh
Josh Gottheimer represents New Jersey’s Fifth Congressional District. Josh is in Congress to fight for lower taxes and Jersey Values. He’s working across the aisle to find real solutions for New Jersey families and is actively fighting against the ideological gridlock in Washington. | Today, on Juneteenth, we celebrate the end of slavery in the United States and honor the rich culture, history, and accomplishments of Black communities across the country.

This year, we honor Juneteenth for the fourth time as a federal holiday after more than a century and a half of pushing for recognition. It's a day for reflection and celebration and a reminder of the ongoing fight for racial justice and equity.

As we commemorate this important day, we recognize that much work still needs to be done. In Congress, I am committed to protecting voting rights, easing environmental injustice, improving healthcare disparities, increasing access to a good education, and so much more in order to create opportunities that uplift communities that need them most. The fight for equality is far from over, but together, we can make meaningful progress.

Our team is looking forward to attending celebrations across the district this week. I hope you'll join me in recommitting to the fight for equality.

Onward,
Sarah Elfreth

This year, we honor Juneteenth for the fourth time as a federal holiday after more than a century and a half of pushing for recognition. It's a day for reflection and celebration and a reminder of the ongoing fight for racial justice and equity. As we commemorate this important day, we recognize that much work still needs to be done. Today, we observe 159 years of Juneteenth, celebrating the liberation and resilience of Black Americans.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87183969/480319840/950179054?refcode=EM_C_240619Juneteenth_N_SB_90DO_5_NG_N_Logo&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMTBiMTcxZi00MjJlLWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7SsYoiWBU2sLaqV_oO7i4MiKxW3TQYcx3rNbfeYZyPM=) Peter,

Today, we observe 159 years of Juneteenth, celebrating the liberation and resilience of Black Americans. On June 19, 1865, the news of freedom finally reached the last emancipated people in Texas, two and a half years after President Abraham Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation, and 159 years later, we are still fighting for equality and justice.

**Juneteenth has always connected past and present – but it is especially important this year. Elected officials are taking Black history, Black literature, and Black studies off the syllabus and banning books on our history and culture from libraries.**

In Congress, I am working to strengthen federal support for Black history education, bolster civil rights protections, and expand economic opportunity for all. Black culture and history are etched into our country’s history and culture – and I am celebrating that powerful sentiment today and every day.

**I hope we all have the opportunity today to immerse ourselves in the strength of our diversity while reflecting on the needs of our Black communities.**

There’s no greater honor than fighting for the rights of my people and every disenfranchised American during this pivotal time in our history.

Gratefully,

Shontel Brown | As a Cuyahoga County Council member and Chairwoman of the Cuyahoga County Democratic Party, Shontel Brown has spent the last decade serving the people of Ohio and building coalitions. Now, as the Congresswoman for Ohio’s 11th District, she will fight for affordable quality health care, jobs that pay fair wages, a strong public education system, and equity and justice for all. **Will you join her and be the change we need?**

# Tennessee Speaker Cameron Sexton wants to turn Memphis red. He might succeed.
---
|
## _Speaker Cameron Sexton's Memphis plan may be aspirational, but not impossible. His opponents should realize that he is dead serious about wanting to extend the GOP's reach firmly across Tennessee._
---
| By: [David Plazas](https://ElectBergmann.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ed4565687fe1f93d61fb32842&id=31ac3d8ab2&e=9dd54a4530)
Nashville Tennessean
Published 9:18 a.m. CT June 18, 2024
David Plazas is the director of opinion and engagement for the USA TODAY Network Tennessee.
---
| Thirty years ago, Republicans won key elections for governor and two U.S. Senate seats that started the state on a path to become deeply politically red.

Congressman Don Sundquist won the governorship after eight years under Democrat Ned McWherter. Dr. Bill Frist defeated incumbent Sen. Jim Sasser. Actor and lawyer Fred Thompson bested former Congressman Jim Cooper in a special election for a seat once held by then-Vice President Al Gore.

Since 1994, only one of four Tennessee governors has been a Democrat, Phil Bredesen, and Republicans have maintained their hold on both Senate seats and developed a super majority in the state legislature.

Meanwhile, only one of nine U.S. House districts is currently held by a Democrat − District 9, represented by Congressman Steve Cohen of Memphis.

**But now, Tennessee Speaker of the House Cameron Sexton says he wants it all.**

At the 47th annual Tennessee Republican Statesmen’s Dinner on June 15, Sexton said: “One day we will turn Memphis red again. And I know that day is coming very soon.”

House Speaker Cameron Sexton, R-Crossville, presents the Legislator of the Year Award to Rep. Mary Littleton, R-Dickson, during the Tennessee Republican Party’s Statesmen’s Dinner at Music City Center in Nashville, Tenn., Saturday, June 15, 2024.

Some might call those comments mere political posturing, but there are already signs that Republicans will try to make good on Sexton's vow.

### **Going after DA Steve Mulroy appears to play into the grand plan.**

Prior to 2023, Tennessee had two Democratic congressional districts. Cohen's Ninth District and the Fifth District, represented for 20 years by Jim Cooper, which used to include all of Nashville, another blue dot in Tennessee's sea of red.

**WITH YOUR HELP, WE WILL WIN, TURN MEMPHIS RED, THUS TURN TENNESSEE RED. **

Fellow American, **I am so grateful for our police officers. ** As an American who believes in law and order, truth, and justice, I have always stood with the public servants who protect our communities. **[Please join me in thanking uniformed men and women by signing our'Back the Blue Petition' and letting brave officers know that we are grateful for their service and sacrifice.](http://trk.libertyledger._c291cmNlX2NvZGU9TExPNTA1MjUifQ/BtYosVfpXmnoCz4f7NCAxw)**

---
Unfortunately, a few years ago, radicals began propelling criminals into heroes overnight and campaigning to "_defund the police_." I refuse to accept that we must cater to the bottom denominator of our society and that the black community must fight and scream and demand support for the people in our community who are up to no good. That's one of the reasons I founded BLEXIT -- an organization focused on shifting the culture in Black America as well as educating and uplifting minorities through educational programs and acts of community service. **Around the nation, our BLEXIT chapters have supported local officers, while so many others have turned their backs on those who serve our communities. ** **[To join these chapters and stand with police officers, please sign the national petition today.](http://trk.libertyledger._c291cmNlX2NvZGU9TExPNTA1MjUifQ/j5IibsuU0yq8C7Z5cdLh4w)**

body:
While we celebrate Juneteenth today, we must also take stock of the work that still needs to be done. | |
---
Happy Juneteenth, Derek. On this day in 1865, Union soldiers arrived in Texas and formally announced the last enslaved people of their freedom, two years after the signing of the Emancipation Proclamation. One hundred and fifty-nine years ago, newly freed slaves didn’t know what awaited them outside of slavery, but they knew they now had the opportunity to pursue a better life for themselves, their families and loved ones, and the next generation. Today, we move forward with that same hope our ancestors had as we continue our fight for a more perfect union, but we also acknowledge the work still ahead of us, and the barriers that remain -- many of which our ancestors faced, too. Systemic racism and white supremacy remain all too prevalent in our society and institutions. There is more we can -- and _must_ \-- do to protect the right to vote and counter the voter suppression laws that all too often target Black communities. We must keep fighting to expand access to affordable health care, to bring down costs, and to defend our hard-won freedoms from those working to dismantle them. Our work continues, Derek, and I’m grateful to have you with us. Thank you, and happy Juneteenth. Jaime Harrison
Chair
Democratic National Committee

name: Tina Smith
subject: I’m thinking of Ms. Opal Lee
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Tina Smith for Minnesota
body:
|
#
Happy Juneteenth, team! Juneteenth marks the end of slavery in America. On June 19th, 1865, a full two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation, Major General Gordon Granger issued General Order No. 3 in Galveston, Texas, which freed the last enslaved Americans. It’s never been more important to recognize our history and commemorate the end of the dark stain of slavery — especially as MAGA Republicans and school boards across the country are trying to erase the importance of the struggle for Black liberation. Try as they might, _they will not wipe away the hard work and persistent fight for freedom._ **Today we remember the countless Black activists who have fought for recognition of Juneteenth, but especially Ms. Opal Lee, known as the grandmother of Juneteenth.** In 2016, at 89 she walked from her home in Fort Worth, Texas, to Washington, bringing with her a petition supporting the creation of a federal holiday in celebration of Juneteenth. I felt a duty to heed her call. I was the leading co-sponsor of the _Juneteenth National Independence Day Act_ , which President Biden signed into law in his first year in office and makes today a nationally recognized federal holiday. After this bill passed the Senate, I had the opportunity to call Ms. Lee. When I told her the good news, the sound of the joy in her voice is a memory I will treasure for the rest of my life. So while we celebrate today, let this also be a moment of rededication to the cause of racial justice. Let us all work diligently toward the systemic change Black people deserve and need — like protecting voting rights and safeguarding our democracy, passing meaningful policing and criminal justice reform, pursuing economic and environmental justice, and working towards a more just and equitable world. I know that lately, the path to justice has felt impossibly long. But even in the darkest moments — let us draw inspiration and strength from the example of these heroes like Ms. Lee, and work together for a future of equity and justice for all. Thank you, Tina

## Celebrating Juneteenth
---
---
On the eve of January 1, 1863, known as "Freedom's Eve," the first Watch Night services saw enslaved and free African Americans gather in anticipation of the Emancipation Proclamation. At midnight, their prayers were answered as all enslaved people in Confederate states were declared legally free, a monumental step for the nation. Union soldiers, many of whom were black, spread the news across the South, but true freedom for all enslaved people only came with the Thirteenth Amendment. In Texas, freedom arrived on June 19, 1865, when Union troops declared the emancipation of over 250,000 enslaved people, a day now celebrated as "Juneteenth." This day marks a pivotal moment in American history, symbolizing the end of slavery and the beginning of a long journey toward equality. The post-emancipation period, known as Reconstruction (1865-1877), was a time of hope and struggle as formerly enslaved people sought to reunify families, establish schools, enter politics, and push for radical legislation. Despite progress being made in many instances, America still faced significant challenges in achieving true equality. Americans are still actively fighting for this push towards equality. Democrats in all 50 states continue this work, recognizing that racism has no place in the land of the free. In 2021, President Biden declared Juneteenth a national holiday to honor its significance and remind Americans of slavery's legacy and the nation's ability to heal and progress. This holiday serves as a reminder that today's challenges are different from those of past generations, but the fight for equality requires the same dedication and vigilance as demonstrated by the heroes of our civil rights history. Juneteenth reminds us of the progress we've made and the work that still lies ahead. Join us as we celebrate the fight for equality and recognize the importance defending equality in the land of the free.

body:
Today on Juneteenth, we commemorate the day in 1865 on which the final enslaved Americans in the confederate South learned they were free.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87188457/480333614/966991095?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTFhNDdmYi00NzJlLWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5-s_pqeT-nNeHjaJtw-vfMZAUNqMNYIOy7X3FGvqM0E=&emci=c42a4c14-ab2d-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=151a47fb-472e-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=43402272) | Peter, Today on Juneteenth, we commemorate the day in 1865 on which the final enslaved Americans in the confederate South learned they were free. Today is only our country's fourth year recognizing Juneteenth as a federal holiday. **It took more than 150 years for America to formally celebrate something as massive as the abolition of slavery — which speaks volumes about the work we have ahead of us.** American history is often told as a simple story of continuous progress. We learn that the Emancipation Proclamation and the 13th Amendment freed slaves and set the country on a path towards equality. But we know it’s not nearly as simple as that. The legacy of slavery in America has been horrific, enduring, and damaging. Following the abolition of slavery came Jim Crow, segregation, and discrimination. Today, the inequities that Black Americans experience in housing, health care, and education are a direct consequence of the racism that was written into America’s laws and policies in the century following the abolition of slavery. There is so much work ahead of us to take responsibility for our racist history, repair the harm caused by it, and dismantle racist systems that continue to negatively impact Black Americans. Today, I will be celebrating Juneteenth by reflecting on what I can do to leverage my own privilege and power to challenge racist systems, uplift the needs and voices of Black Vermonters, and continue making progress – real progress – towards our vision of liberty and justice for all. Have a joyous Juneteenth, Peter. Becca Balint

There is so much work ahead of us to take responsibility for our racist history, repair the harm caused by it, and dismantle racist systems that continue to negatively impact Black Americans. Today, I will be celebrating Juneteenth by reflecting on what I can do to leverage my own privilege and power to challenge racist systems, uplift the needs and voices of Black Vermonters, and continue making progress – real progress – towards our vision of liberty and justice for all. Have a joyous Juneteenth, Peter. More than two years after president Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation: **Happy Juneteenth, Peter!**

On this day in 1865, Union soldiers arrived in Galveston, Texas, to announce the end of the Civil War and the freedom of all enslaved people – _more than two years after President Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation._

Juneteenth serves as a powerful testament to the progress we’ve made in the fight for liberation and equality – **but it is also a stark reminder for all of us that there is still much more we must do to realize the promise of a country where people are _truly_ equal. **

This year, let us come together as a community to honor the resilience and contributions of Black Americans throughout history. Whether through local events, conversations with loved ones, or personal reflection, **I hope you’ll join me in observing Juneteenth and reaffirm your commitment to building a more inclusive and just nation for ALL.**

Onward,

It’s a fight to return true leadership, integrity, and commitment to our country back to the People’s House.
It’s a fight to defend the very future of our democracy, and the stakes have never been higher.

For the past 38 years, Jonathan Emord has litigated against the federal bureaucracy, winning repeatedly. He is a leading constitutional law and litigation expert and the author of five critically acclaimed books.
It's time to end transitioning of youth; stop the assault on girls and women's sports, locker rooms, and bathrooms; eliminate woke indoctrination in schools and the military; ensure equal justice under law; secure our borders; roll back excessive government spending and cut taxes; reduce the size and scope of the government; and liberate free enterprise.

# [#]
Peter,

Today is Juneteenth, a day to commemorate when the last enslaved Black Americans were informed of their freedom in Galveston, Texas – a full two years after the signing of the Emancipation Proclamation.

2024 will mark the first year that Juneteenth is recognized as an official state holiday here in Rhode Island, despite having been a federal holiday for three years. This is an important step to acknowledge our past and highlight the progress we've made toward creating a more equal and just world. There is still work to be done.

Celebrating Juneteenth this year – and every year – It is a reminder of how hard we’ve worked to ensure that all Americans will have their rights respected – and how much farther we still have to go. Let’s reflect today on our past and continue working towards a better future — ensuring that we are an accepting and fair nation, advocating for each and every American.

Thank you,

Seth
