body:
And is one of the reasons why I’m fighting for universal healthcare.
# [](https://act.hillharper.com/go/421?t=1&akid=1272%2E62735%2E-24Jnh)
Hey, Peter —
**I wanted to take a moment to share a deeply personal story with you —** one that has shaped not only my own perspective but also my commitment to fighting for transformative change for our country’s healthcare system. It’s a longer email, so I hope you’ll take the time to read it.
Back in 2010, while filming in Atlanta, I woke up one morning unable to swallow. A sore throat had escalated into something far more serious, leading me to seek medical attention.
Little did I know that this visit would change the course of my life.
**After an immediate biopsy and a tense wait for results, I received news that I had cancer — the same disease that had taken the lives of my father, grandfather, and uncle.** It was a sobering moment for me, one that forced me to confront my mortality and the fragility of my own life.
But I refused to let fear consume me. With the support of my loved ones and the guidance of skilled medical professionals, I underwent surgery to remove my thyroid gland and embarked on a journey toward recovery. **Today, I am grateful to say that I am cancer-free and blessed with a clean bill of health.**
My own brush with cancer opened my eyes to the harsh realities faced by too many Americans. I've seen firsthand the devastating toll that sky-high medical costs can take on individuals and their loved ones. I've witnessed the crippling burden of medical debt, which can shatter dreams of the future and push families to the brink of financial ruin. And while I was fortunate to receive financial assistance from my union, I know that not everyone is so lucky.
**That's why I pledge to fight like hell for universal healthcare access for ALL Americans, regardless of the circumstances.** No one should have to endure the stress of choosing between their health and financial stability. No one should fear for their family’s future while they should be focusing on treatment and recovery. And no one, in the wealthiest nation in the history of the world, should go bankrupt just for seeking the lifesaving care they need.
**[So today, I’m humbly asking for your support. Will you please chip in any amount — even $5 or $10 — to help us win this critical Senate race, take our voices to the halls of power, and make universal healthcare a reality in America?](https://act.hillharper.com/go/1733?t=2&akid=1272%2E62735%2E-24Jnh)**

clean_body: And is one of the reasons why I’m fighting for universal healthcare. Hey, Peter — I wanted to take a moment to share a deeply personal story with you — one that has shaped not only my own perspective but also my commitment to fighting for transformative change for our country’s healthcare system. It’s a longer email, so I hope you’ll take the time to read it. Back in 2010, while filming in Atlanta, I woke up one morning unable to swallow. A sore throat had escalated into something far more serious, leading me to seek medical attention. Little did I know that this visit would change the course of my life. After an immediate biopsy and a tense wait for results, I received news that I had cancer — the same disease that had taken the lives of my father, grandfather, and uncle. It was a sobering moment for me, one that forced me to confront my mortality and the fragility of my own life. But I refused to let fear consume me. With the support of my loved ones and the guidance of skilled medical professionals, I underwent surgery to remove my thyroid gland and embarked on a journey toward recovery. Today, I am grateful to say that I am cancer-free and blessed with a clean bill of health. My own brush with cancer opened my eyes to the harsh realities faced by too many Americans. I've seen firsthand the devastating toll that sky-high medical costs can take on individuals and their loved ones. I've witnessed the crippling burden of medical debt, which can shatter dreams of the future and push families to the brink of financial ruin. And while I was fortunate to receive financial assistance from my union, I know that not everyone is so lucky. That's why I pledge to fight like hell for universal healthcare access for ALL Americans, regardless of the circumstances. No one should have to endure the stress of choosing between their health and financial stability. No one should fear for their family’s future while they should be focusing on treatment and recovery. And no one, in the wealthiest nation in the history of the world, should go bankrupt just for seeking the lifesaving care they need. Together, we can build a healthier, more equitable Michigan — and a stronger, more compassionate nation. Thank you for your support, Hill Harper Democrat for U.S. Senate

body:
[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/62?t=1001&akid=6730%2E5257348%2E4YQYmT ]Adam Schiff for Senate

It’s an understatement to say that the House of Representatives under
Republican control is a disaster.

Bills don’t get passed to help citizens as they struggle with inflation
and the cost of living. Reproductive freedom is eroded day after day. The
Supreme Court green-lights the gun lobby again and again and Americans pay
with their lives.

Respect for government is at an all-time low as Republican members like
Majorie Taylor Greene degrade our institutions like never before.

Vile performance art has substituted for law-making as the GOP battle for
who can appease Donald Trump the most with varying acts of fealty — from
suggesting he serve as Speaker of the House to suggesting the House
expunge his impeachment.

Derek, if there’s
anyone who knows to what level Republicans will stoop to, it’s me.

Every single day, I face personal attacks from MAGA Republicans calling me
“shifty,” “watermelon head,” “pencil neck,” and anything else they’ve
heard from the mouth of their criminal leader.

But even worse than the personal attacks, which I will gladly accept if
that’s the price for defending our democracy, was what happened just one
year ago.

My censure.

What was originally reserved for flagrant violations of the law or
personal behavior unbefitting of a member of Congress is now frequently
being used by Republicans to attack people they disagree with.

I will never regret my work to investigate the former president for his
efforts to destroy our democracy. While Republicans under Donald Trump’s
command attack me for holding him accountable, I will not back down. Not
now. Not ever.

On this day in 1865, news of the Emancipation Proclamation finally reached the enslaved Black people of Galveston, Texas.
Happy Juneteenth, team!

On this day in 1865, news of the Emancipation Proclamation finally reached the enslaved Black people of Galveston, Texas—two years after its issuance. That day, the last remaining enslaved people in the U.S. learned they were free, and we marked the end of a very dark period in our nation’s history.
Juneteenth is a reminder of the bondage that our nation inflicted upon Black people, and the joy felt by the newly freed people on that day. Despite how far we’ve come, we can’t honor this holiday without acknowledging how far we still have to go in the fight for equality in our country—159 years later.

From the ballot box to our criminal legal system to education, systemic racism still remains pervasive in our society. **Black Americans are still fighting for equality and equity under the law.**

As one of the first Black, gay members of Congress, I’m proud of the work I did to fight for equality and equity for _every_ American, including passing legislation to make today a national holiday. But there’s still more work to be done and I’m ready to get back to Congress to keep fighting.

So today, please join me in recommitting to upholding freedom and justice for all in our country.

Thank you,

Mondaire

Nadarius Clark, who we helped get elected to the Virginia House of Delegates, just got his gun safety bill passed and signed!
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20240619&t=1&akid=825%2E587540%2E_UvmaA)
Peter, huge news from Leaders We Deserve’s first elected candidate:
**Nadarius Clark, who we helped get elected to the Virginia House of Delegates, just got his gun safety bill passed and signed — by a Republican governor, no less!**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240619-1?refcode=em20240619-1&amount=5&refcode2=825_587540__UvmaA&akid=825%2E587540%2E_UvmaA)
[**Will you make an immediate donation of $5 to Leaders We Deserve so we can elect even more inspirational young leaders like Nadarius this November?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240619-1?refcode=em20240619-1&amount=5&refcode2=825_587540__UvmaA&akid=825%2E587540%2E_UvmaA)
Stopping gun violence is one of the _biggest reasons_ Nadarius ran for office in the first place, and he knew that even with a Republican governor in office, _something had to be done_.
**Nadarius wasn’t willing to sit around and wait years for a Democratic governor with a spine to replace the NRA-backed Republican currently in office,** so he started thinking about what he could get done under the current circumstances.
He landed on a bill that offers tax credits to gun owners who buy gun locks and safes, so that no gun owner faces a financial barrier to keep their weapons safe and out of the reach of kids and others who shouldn’t be able to get them.
Look, I get it — this may not be everything we wanted, but if even one life is saved as a result of this bill, it was worth it. And you can bet that when the current NRA-backed governor is replaced with a Democrat who’s willing to keep our communities safe, **Nadarius will be there leading the charge to do even more.**
What makes all this even more impressive is that Nadarius is the _youngest person_ serving in the Virginia legislature, and his district is the most competitive in the entire state.
Last year we gave Nadarius’ campaign about $100,000, and **he won by just about 800 votes**. That secured a 1 seat majority in the House of Delegates which enabled him to pass this law _and_ kill a separate GOP bill that sought to arm teachers.
It’s clear to me that this work is making a difference — but as a grassroots organization that doesn’t take corporate donations, we’re counting on your support to keep going.
[**We’ve endorsed 13 more candidates for this year’s elections, Peter. Will you pitch in $5 right now to support our work so they can win their elections and start making a difference just like Nadarius?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240619-1?refcode=em20240619-1&amount=5&refcode2=825_587540__UvmaA&akid=825%2E587540%2E_UvmaA)

Thank you,
David Hogg

name: Team Baccam
subject: “just a little old lady in tennis shoes getting in everybody’s business”
body:
www.lanonbaccam.com [www.lanonbaccam.com]
Happy Juneteenth, Peter!

This is the third year our nation collectively recognizes the date, June 19, 1865, that the southernmost enslaved Americans in Galveston, TX, learned of their freedom — more than two years after Lincoln’s Emancipation Proclamation.

Juneteenth is, of course, about celebrating freedom and hard-fought progress. But our work is not done. Protecting our democracy and freedoms requires us to continually engage with each other.

Opal Lee, the Grandmother of Juneteenth, fought for the true story head-on in 2016 when she, at age 89 , marched the 1,400 miles from her home in Fort Worth, Texas, to Washington, D.C., advocating for the federal recognition of Juneteenth.

Ms. Lee often refers to herself as “just a little old lady in tennis shoes getting in everybody’s business.”

Maybe she is. But Peter, we need more folks in tennis shoes fighting to bring justice and elevate our nation to a higher moral standard — just like Opal.

People of color, and Black Americans especially, continue facing inequalities today. And it is only through our collective action, our advocacy, and our marching shoes that we will enact lasting progress for all of us.

Opal Lee is a 97-year-old retired teacher who continues to inspire lasting advocacy, Peter. It shows the impact that ordinary people can have just by standing up.

Have a happy and meaningful Juneteenth, Peter!

— Team Baccam

name: Ro Khanna
subject: BREAKING: Historically Black Colleges and Universities are at risk of closing
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ro for Congress
body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]

Friend,

Juneteenth is a celebration of freedom. It’s a celebration of independence. It’s a celebration of emancipation. It commemorates the day enslaved people were declared free in Texas in 1865 – three years after President Lincoln’s emancipation proclamation.

Our newest federal holiday reminds us of how far we’ve come as a nation and how far we still have to go to achieve a more perfect union.

For over 200 years, Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) in the nation, such as Claflin, Morehouse, Howard, and Spelman, have been critical to the American story.

But right now, HBCUs are at risk of funding cuts and closure. In Mississippi, a state senator recently proposed legislation that would put three of the state’s HBCUs at risk of closure and disproportionately harm Black students across the state.

Sign if you agree: We must support Historically Black Colleges and Universities. [https://actionnetwork.org/forms/save-hbcus-show-your-support-by-signing-on-now/?source=group-ro-khanna&referrer=group-ro-khanna&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Frise-hbcu-swap]

Today, communities across the U.S. will celebrate the anniversary of the end of chattel slavery in the South. Juneteenth is America's most recently established federal holiday, but it--and the impact of the historical events that it celebrates--are also widely misunderstood.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e759408d-86d4-426f-a568-70e0ea074767?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Image Source: publicdomainpictures.net
Last year, I published "[Juneteenth remains aspirational](https://substack.com/redirect/0a905079-6710-4fb9-b8e8-6b3880fffac0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" in order to remind readers of several points obscured by congratulatory celebrations that overlook our nation's reprehensible--and continuing--history, including:
* the actual impact of the Emancipation Proclamation at the time that Lincoln issued it;
* the meaning of the 13th Amendment that ended the Civil War, and a critical caveat that has allowed slavery to not only fester, but also to expand across the United States and grow multiracial;
* President Biden's self-serving hypocrisy in recognizing Juneteenth as a national holiday;
* the perverse political co-optation of communities who today celebrate a supposed history that unfortunately remains an object of hope; and
* a link between incarceration and economics overlooked even by most people who do recognize contemporary mass slavery across the United States.

## [Juneteenth remains aspirational](https://substack.com/redirect/0a905079-6710-4fb9-b8e8-6b3880fffac0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[Described by the Smithsonian as "our nation's second Independence Day," Juneteenth is the most recent federal holiday to gain formal recognition. It commemorates the approximate date--more than two years after President Lincoln declared the Emancipation Proclamation](https://substack.com/redirect/0a905079-6710-4fb9-b8e8-6b3880fffac0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

As I [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/0a905079-6710-4fb9-b8e8-6b3880fffac0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last year:
> The notion that Biden would claim any credit for enshrining Juneteenth as a national holiday is frankly grotesque when considered in light of his policy record as a Senator before [weaseling](https://substack.com/redirect/8644a879-7718-4e17-8b48-a45f25b2b492?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his way into the White House. He was the author of the 1993 crime bill that notoriously [swelled](https://substack.com/redirect/ecf5e99c-2df6-4c77-aa1d-0f762dc53118?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the ranks of our nation's prisons, as well as the [quarterback](https://substack.com/redirect/18accf4d-e431-4af2-9e5a-a8ce8e234fbe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the process that put Clarence Thomas on the Supreme Court--reflecting yet again Biden's long history of theatrical nods to the concerns of Black communities while ignoring their needs and interests in practice.
> ...
> By all means, celebrate Juneteenth. But don't pretend that slavery ever ended in the United States.

name: Debbie Mucarsel-Powell
subject: 159 years ago today
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Debbie for Florida
body:
Today is a celebration of one of our greatest moments of liberation.
| | | Friend,

**On this day in 1865, word finally made it to Black Americans still in bondage in Texas that they were free, and that they had been since the Emancipation Proclamation was issued over two years earlier.**
---
159 years later, Americans of all colors now celebrate, honor, and reflect on this moment as Juneteenth National Independence Day.
Believe it or not, Florida was one of the first states to commemorate Juneteenth as a day of observance back in 1991.****
**But right now, I’m not sure whether our Republican leaders would allow the true reason for this federal holiday to be properly taught in school** — and that’s sickening, friend.
What’s more — due to our extremist GOP leaders' efforts to:
* Censor or entirely exclude Black people and history from American history in our public education system
* Sign various anti-civil rights and voting rights measures into law
* Criminalize protests
* Dismantle diversity and inclusion measures in the public sphere
* Blatantly devalue and marginalize the contributions of and challenges faced by Black Americans and other marginalized communities, and more

— the NAACP has issued a travel advisory to Black Americans and other marginalized groups for Florida. **The sad truth that _anyone_ would have to worry about safely traveling to my home state is wholly unacceptable.**
And the fact that Florida has the second largest Black population among all 50 states — and yet some of the **worst** racial disparities in health outcomes, maternal and infant mortality rates, household incomes, home ownership, university enrollment, and incarceration rates, _which have only worsened since Rick Scott was elected governor in 2010_ —**is downright reprehensible.**
All of this reflects the backward direction that both Ron DeSantis and his predecessor, Rick Scott, have steered Florida in across their tenures.
It's one of the reasons why my campaign slogan is _ya no más:**B****ecause enough is enough.**_
As Florida's next senator, I will fight to grow opportunities for Black-owned small businesses, expand voting rights, and combat our state's skyrocketing Black maternal mortality rates. Enough is enough.
I'll fight for all Floridians to enjoy the liberty, justice, and equal opportunities promised by the American Dream. Enough is enough.
And I'll never stop fighting back against the hate-fueled regime that's taken over the Sunshine State and worked tirelessly to crack down on the health, history, and freedoms of our Black community members. _**Enough is enough.**_
We must stand strong in our fight for justice. Democracy will not die on our watch, and together this November, we will set Florida back on the path of prosperity and justice for all our communities. **Until then, I am overjoyed to join the celebration of one of our nation's greatest moments of liberation.**
Happy Juneteenth.
In solidarity,

Debbie

Peter, this Juneteenth, I'm thinking about how far our fight for true freedom and equality for African Americans has come – and how far we still have to go.

**Sometimes it's hard to wrap my head around how much progress we've made in just a couple of generations.**

I grew up during segregation. In North Carolina, we could not eat in the same restaurants as white people. When we went to the grocery store, we were taught not to look directly at a white person. **Almost everything was separate, nothing was equal.**

When I was 13 years old, I went to school with white kids for the first time. I finally had new books for the first time, as opposed to the worn-out ones we were accustomed to before. But, the integration of Black students into white society was far from equitable.

We conducted sit-ins and protests to fight for a Black marshall at graduation, the allowance of Black cheerleaders on the squad, reliable school bus schedules for Black students, and more. The progress was slow, but my peers and I persevered, fighting for what we deserved.

**As we commemorate the emancipation of enslaved Black people in America on Juneteenth, we also celebrate the progress we have made and will continue to make for future generations.**

The progress we see today is a culmination of concerted efforts across the United States by Black advocates to create a better life. Every single act, big or small, has contributed to the changes we see today.

Instead of conditioning my children to avoid eye contact, I taught them to look people in the eye and greet them with a firm handshake and a smile. The truth is, we have more in common with others than we have differences.

But, there are still systemic issues stemming from slavery and segregation. There is still plenty to do. So today, we celebrate how far we’ve come in our fight for racial justice and equality – and tomorrow we continue our mission.

Thank you for taking a moment to reflect on Juneteenth with me.

— Valerie Foushee

| | On January 1st, 1863, President Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation, effectively freeing more than three and a half million enslaved people throughout the United States. But word didn’t reach the people of Galveston, Texas until June 19th, 1865 — _two and a half years later._ A century and half later, we remember our ancestors and the travesties and injustices they faced, and we celebrate their courage in fighting for a better future they’d never get to see. Their struggle is one they never should have been forced to endure. But they knew that their dream of a better world for their children and grandchildren was — _and always will be_ — worth fighting for. When I think about what Juneteenth means to me and my family, I think about my great-grandmother, Maebel James. She was born in the segregated South, just 31 years after the first Juneteenth, and she faced unspeakable tragedy in her life. Our family eventually fled the South and came to Maryland. While my sister and I were growing up, Maebel was always there, a testament to empathy, resilience, and dignity. Peter, she was so proud when I entered law school. I know the fact that I’m now the Democratic nominee to represent Maryland in the U.S. Senate would mean the world to her. Maebel witnessed our country change and transform — sometimes for the better, other times not — and she faced it all with grace, empathy, and love. To me, she’ll always embody the same resilience, strength, and boundless hope that we recognize today on Juneteenth. We’ve still got a long way to go, Peter, but progress demands that we’re active, not passive, in the righteous struggle for justice, equality, and opportunity. Together, Angela Alsobrooks [](https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/27030?t=7&amount=25&akid=1876%2E52803%2Ei6aDZd)

name: Sarah McBride
subject: Happy Juneteenth
body:
It’s a celebration of emancipation and freedom as well as a reminder that our freedoms must be actively defended if they’re to remain a reality.
#
June 19th, 1865 is a monumental day in our nation’s history. And while Juneteenth may have only been recognized as a federal holiday a few years ago, Americans around the country have marked it for over a century.
It’s the day Union soldiers arrived in Houston, TX — then the last stronghold of the Confederacy — with the news that President Lincoln had decreed all enslaved African Americans throughout the country to be free.
Because while the Emancipation Proclamation technically went into effect on January 1, 1863, the reality is that it took more than two years for freedom to reach all parts of the country in practice.
So today, I hope you’ll join me in celebrating this monumental holiday. It’s a celebration of emancipation and freedom as well as a reminder that our freedoms must be actively defended if they’re to remain a reality — an important reminder in today’s world.
Happy Juneteenth,
Sarah McBride

Our country continues to deny Black people equal rights, and now right-wing groups and federal courts are attacking affirmative action and reparations programs. Oklahoma’s top court just took away the chance for reparations to survivors of the 1921 Tulsa Race Massacre. **We need to support some of the fiercest champions in Congress for racial justice: Cori Bush and Jamaal Bowman.** These progressive Black leaders are fighting back against anti-Black racism and demanding reinvestments and reparations for Black communities. **They’re up for re-election soon and they’re facing primary challengers who are taking millions of dollars from racist MAGA billionaires.** Cori and Jamaal’s opponents are endorsed and funded by the right-wing group AIPAC, which has a pattern of interfering in Democratic primary elections to try to defeat Black and brown progressives. Today, on Juneteenth, I am reminded of the profound importance this day holds in our nation's history. | | | [](http://links.mullenformontana.com/u/click?_t=96962950e68f455895e83c6431fce0d7&_m=482623f34ac74ff4ab74f601b035b18f&_e=bYLMRR4oJiP8HcmCZ1QIX3qafhE_3SrvzCQZMlNbUlM7r_4ISCV9663TiLyq_UcGUWpC8EKNqdPnXg4DLbHPebxA4UXt3R295jsB8O61TEK4cNtNGy-iAFkZI2V1g8GapuMx82WtpChXQwN6ePgG9ckEEg7XcAQGgohbTH9fr2RC03hE3QOYMGdmm6eiC5Y7NFRr5DuwJ58bLsmvXPybzQ%3D%3D) Folks, Today, on Juneteenth, I am reminded of the profound importance this day holds in our nation's history. We’re celebrating the emancipation of enslaved African Americans in Texas on June 19, 1865, which, for you history buffs, **is over two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was signed.** Montana may not be the first place that comes to mind when you think of African American history, but like so many states, ours has a rich and often overlooked legacy. From the brave Black soldiers who served at Fort Missoula to the vibrant African American communities that grew and thrived in places like Helena and Great Falls, our history is deeply interwoven with the contributions and struggles of African Americans. As Secretary of State, I am committed to doing what I can to move forward in the fight for racial equality. Whether it be fighting against voter suppression tactics to ensure every eligible voter has access to the polls, or improving our business processes to make it easier for minority business owners to succeed, I will stand strong in pushing our state more equal and just. So as we celebrate Juneteenth, we must acknowledge the past and commit to building a future where every Montanan can thrive. All the best, Jesse James Mullen Paid for by Mullen For Secretary of State

Today is not only a day of celebration but also a time for reflection.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87197990/480364994/-1747597063?nd&amount=10&refcode=em_fr_2024.06.19_b1_es_all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85NTEyNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNjFjZmRmNy01NDJlLWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=YYHvGXMDDpVzgtOAY6vnixOG2Ee3zWSxZJjJX3XdTHg=) Happy Juneteenth! Today is not only a day of celebration but also a time for reflection. It is a time to recognize how far we have come and how far we have to go. On June 19, 1865, only 159 years ago, the last enslaved people in Texas got the news that they were free. Since then, generations before us have fought tooth and nail for desegregation, voting rights, equal treatment, and so much more. **This day is a reminder of the resilience of the Black community.** Every day, I am inspired and motivated by the drive of those who came before me with even more obstacles to face. Shirley Chisholm, John Lewis, and Sojourner Truth, just to name a few. Their courage paved the way for progress, and it is essential for us to drive that progress forward each and every day. More than a celebration of freedom, Juneteenth is a reminder that we have to actively work towards dismantling racism and injustice in our society as well as advocate for policies that promote inclusion and equity. As we honor and celebrate Juneteenth, let us all remember that the fight for freedom, equality, and inclusion must continue. Happy Juneteenth! _Emilia Sykes_

| **A native of Akron, Ohio, Emilia Sykes has deep roots fighting for Ohioans. She learned from a young age how to use her voice and the power of the people to create change.** **In 2022, Congresswoman Sykes was elected to represent Ohio’s newly redrawn 13th Congressional District, winning one of the toughest races in the country._Emilia has cut through the divisiveness to deliver results._ **

Friend,
Populism
is nothing new to world history. While it can be easy to think
about American politics as being divided between the Left and the
Right, the reality is much different. What we've really been
seeing is two sets of populist backlash against both the Democrat
and Republican establishment.

And
believe it or not, these tensions actually trace their roots back
to Roman times.

That's
why I'm sending you this email today.

I want to
make sure you get a free copy of one of our popular eBooks:
Dueling Populisms by Victor Davis Hanson.

Hanson is
a Hoover Senior Fellow and world-renowned historian, and I think
you'll get a lot out of his insights. Inside this important
eBook, you'll learn more about:

What
we can expect from a political climate ruled by movements that
rebel against both the establishment-and each other.
The
important parallels between these ancient movements and their
modern counterparts in both progressive and conservative
populism.
What
lies ahead for America as we revive these ancient tensions in our
culture.

You can
get your free copy of Dueling Populisms using this secure link:
https://resources.hoover.org/dueling-populisms-signup/.

please feel free to share this with your family and friends. It's
important that we recall the voices of experience and apply them
to contemporary conflicts and challenges.

Today on Juneteenth, we commemorate the freeing of the last enslaved people in the United States, which happened on this day in 1865.

| Peter,

Today on Juneteenth, we commemorate the freeing of the last enslaved people in the United States, which happened on this day in 1865 – more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was issued.

Juneteenth is a reminder that real and lasting change won’t happen overnight and is an important opportunity to look clear-eyed at the state of our democracy right now. We must pay close attention to the ongoing battles for fairness, equity, and meaningful representation at every level of our government. _**And we must act to ensure that Black voices are heard and uplifted in the halls of power.**_

As Emerge’s first Black woman president, I’m proud to lead an organization dedicated to changing the face of power, politics, and leadership in our country – so we can achieve policies that address the lived experience of all our communities. To that end, we must empower more Black women to lead at every level of office – from school boards to the U.S. Congress – and continue to support committed changemakers in our communities across the South.

Emerge is critical to this mission. We have 213 Black alums proudly serving in office right now, and we tirelessly train more bold women of the New American Majority to run and win. That’s why we launched our Seated Together program, our first-in-the-nation advanced candidate leadership program for Black women elected officials who aspire to run for higher office. Our third Seated Together cohort is happening right now, and our team is working to recruit more women for the program on a daily basis to ensure more Black women are at the helm at every level of government.

Our work is far from over, but by continuing to build our movement, Emerge is advancing the fight for real representation so that all our communities can thrive.

Thank you for being a part of this crucial work.

Standing with you,

A’shanti F. Gholar
President, Emerge

body:
Today is a day to celebrate emancipation and the progress we have made since 1865. However, we mustn't forget the path still ahead.
# [](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/388?refcode=em20240619-9134-header&t=1&akid=9134%2E434096%2E2TZDy6)
Derek,
Today is a day to celebrate emancipation and the progress we as a nation have made since 1865. However, we mustn't forget the path still ahead.
This Juneteenth, I am reflecting on the long shadow of systemic racism in America. The statistics don’t lie about the effects of this shadow on Black Americans today.
Studies show that Black Americans are statistically more likely to:
* Experience a violent encounter with law enforcement.1
* Face harsher sentencing.2
* Have shorter life expectancies than their white counterparts.3

When I entered the Senate, I made a commitment to work towards building a more just and fair nation. Our work continues and lives depend on it.
PA always stands by the unshakeable truth that **Black families matter + Black lives matter.**
In solidarity,
❤️ John
John Fetterman
U.S. Senator from Pennsylvania

body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/lizzie-reelect-logo-outlined.png]
Today, we celebrate Juneteenth and all it represents, here in Texas and across the country.
Juneteenth has special significance for Texans because on this day in 1865—more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was issued—Texans received word of the end of slavery in the U.S. when Maj. Gen. Gordon Granger arrived in Galveston and announced that all slaves were now free and had “absolute equality” of personal rights and property rights.
Since that day, Texans have celebrated June 19 as a day of freedom, progress, and hope. At the same time, we also know that we still have much work to do to make the promise of this day a reality for all. It is important to remember and learn from our history—all of it—and to work together every day to ensure the promise of America for all of its citizens.
Juneteenth is a celebration of our ability to do that—to advance the cause of freedom, to expand opportunity, and to make progress.
Today is a day of joy and hope and faith that, with perseverance and commitment, we can continue to build a better America for all Americans. To do so, we must know our history and commit ourselves to our ideals of freedom, equality, and opportunity for all Americans. Today and every day.
Together, we can do anything,

| Peter — On Juneteenth — June 19, 1865 — we celebrated the end of slavery in the United States, two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation. **“None of us are free until we’re all free.” – Ms. Opal Lee, Grandmother of Juneteenth** Today is a celebration of independence, justice, and joy, but it also comes with the recognition that Black Americans continue to face inequality. We can honor the history of progress with celebration and with the commitment to continuing the fight. Freedom requires sustained action and a commitment to equality. The wave of Black history bans across the United States in recent years are not only racist attacks on Black communities, but also our public education. As an advocate for equality and justice, I know that we cannot let our history be forgotten. On this Juneteenth, I hope you will join me in reflecting on our nation’s history, and the work we have ahead of us to build the America that we know can exist, not as a dream, but as a reality. Because when we remember, we do better, Peter. — Austin Davis

clean_body: Freedom requires sustained action and a commitment to equality. | | Peter — On Juneteenth — June 19, 1865 — we celebrated the end of slavery in the United States, two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation. “None of us are free until we’re all free.” – Ms. Opal Lee, Grandmother of Juneteenth Today is a celebration of independence, justice, and joy, but it also comes with the recognition that Black Americans continue to face inequality. We can honor the history of progress with celebration and with the commitment to continuing the fight. Freedom requires sustained action and a commitment to equality. The wave of Black history bans across the United States in recent years are not only racist attacks on Black communities, but also our public education. As an advocate for equality and justice, I know that we cannot let our history be forgotten. On this Juneteenth, I hope you will join me in reflecting on our nation’s history, and the work we have ahead of us to build the America that we know can exist, not as a dream, but as a reality. Because when we remember, we do better, Peter. — Austin Davis PAID FOR MY FRIENDS OF AUSTIN DAVIS Emails like this are the most effective way to grow our campaign and reach supporters like you. This Juneteenth, we celebrate the accolades of Black Americans across the country.

The Collective PAC reaffirms our ongoing commitment to building Black political power across the United States. Impactful support means backing Black candidates who unapologetically strive to bring meaningful change to the office and to our communities.

While fighting against constant threats to reduce and whitewash Black history from the GOP, it is essential to be unwavering in our stance. And while we celebrate our accomplishments, our work to tackle voter suppression, police brutality, mass incarceration, environmental racism, redlining, gerrymandering, and so much more is still in progress.

As we celebrate Juneteenth, let us honor the enduring spirit and resilience of Black Americans, recognizing the profound significance of freedom and equality in our nation's history.

Thank you,

The Collective PAC

Friend, freedom requires sustained action and a renewed commitment to equality. Holidays like Juneteenth serve as reminders for us to reflect on history and progress but also to continue the fight onward. Because all Americans deserve the protection of equal rights.

That’s exactly my commitment while in Congress: I will always advocate for the justice, peace, and equity that Black Americans deserve.

Happy Juneteenth, team!

That’s why at One Pennsylvania, **we’re deeply engaged in our community and build long lasting relationships to create the sustainable infrastructure that has a real impact on our lives.** This election is critical to democracy and the lives of frontline communities. Our work to build Black political power is key to winning, because Black people have always played a fundamental part in the struggle for progress in this country, and because our role in this election is vital. _**[Can you chip in now to power this urgent work?](https://click.everyaction.com/k/87201001/480375307/18948178?refcode=EM_FL_OPA_20240619_onb_onb1_cm_pb_ntl_frs_l1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzY2MTk3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI5NTY3ZmRiLTU4MmUtZWYxMS04NmQyLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=f66VjLBF_9bunu82FkjXm3Vr8GIaZnTPYmMPgLHgocA=)**_ | [CHIP IN →](https://click.everyaction.com/k/87201002/480375308/18948178?refcode=EM_FL_OPA_20240619_onb_onb1_cm_pb_ntl_frs_sbt&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzY2MTk3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI5NTY3ZmRiLTU4MmUtZWYxMS04NmQyLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=f66VjLBF_9bunu82FkjXm3Vr8GIaZnTPYmMPgLHgocA=)

Here’s a reminder of what’s at stake:
* Having clean air and water in our neighborhoods
* Saving our communities from gun violence
* Lifting families out of poverty and away from mass incarceration
* Addressing the housing crisis and making sure everyone has a place to live
* Stopping pervasive white supremacy and anti-blackness
* Defending our voting rights and democracy
* Protecting the rights of workers and fixing the rising costs of living — from housing to groceries to gas to childcare and more

Corporations and right-wing extremists don’t want us to succeed. **Billionaires have already poured money to defeat champions for our community, like Rep. Summer Lee, but we invested time in the community, fought back, and won.**

**Official Note From the 70th Secretary of State Mike Pompeo:**

[](https://links.fullmagnews.com/u/click?_t=959d0fa54cad47baa4213176314ae733&_m=23d19d2e5c5d43fc810375cc742462e5&_e=L-vluVBHbe8IZ_ZpG3sKDzncxXZ2zKsZmfq7j4z9Ifi34m3aexJSle3bZET_e2x_JjcKZR71-38pH0xlH1n0CPclYBAfwi0sqVFa2bLaXkOI-KRN8pO5b6ffp-Ahcgm506uv4HkDPUBluCLVwY4S6Br13-EDn_S3UtC-u6raOJeRiZ524Nq5pVRxTHqvjiSIFdWyzubgjNsTNZSVrj23okNZLo4E2aUg1n2lYqILf_KnvXsmkC_koHsR6ZVjBaU5vFOtXciW1cqISKw4YTrATCQJk_3LHnOxK3PauvCfCGUp645USfZN-CKWick7hsDDelajSdcA8cYsPZ-ijqnrDVw5N5_rpJ1Qnhuq0I2Fg7JL2Yro1AxYzMm5-C1jmYjGOO7ru7bsYN_bHpworyrbJA6F7K1Su64hcVn79Rvs8CN9osWH1yRW7WYFP9BunT9UJCzBM-b5n80n-dY6EJ5Md3Y6MAWtNoIsscT3tVl51-YDnuVCvYDRr2eenSC2r3ZL)
This message is an urgent and heartfelt plea to all grassroots American Patriots.

We've been hoping for a huge response to this message, but it hasn't happened.

Everything will be decided by what happens today.

Joe Biden and the Radical Democrats have driven America into the ground. Right now, we see:

_-MILLIONS of illegal immigrants pouring across the border.

-CRIME destroying America's cities.

-INFLATION erasing the American Dream for our kids.

-WAR threatening the security of our allies & the world._

As the 70th U.S. Secretary of State in the Trump Administration, I know what kind of leadership is needed to save our country.

But I'm terrified to see what happens if this request fails.

Joe Biden and the Democrat Political Machine have over **$100 MILLION** in the bank to destroy every single Republican candidate on the map. The House Majority is down to just a few seats.

The Democrats have been racking up election wins and just flipped a red House seat BLUE. They are mobilized, organized, and endlessly funded.

Biden also has the Liberal Media on his side. And the Big Tech companies. And the Huge Labor Unions. And the Left-Wing mega donors, like George Soros.

That's why I'm joining fellow conservative leader, ret. Fighter Pilot & Republican Rep. Jake Ellzey from Texas to reach out to the most dedicated conservatives in America.

Can Jake and I count on you to step up today?

| Immediate ReleaseJune 20th, 2024Contact: Zach BrownEmail: [zach@trpconsulting.org](mailto:zach@trpconsulting.org)

### **Dalila Epperson Announces Endorsement from Local Business Owner and Community Leader Carina Powers**
---
| Monterey County, CA – Dalila Epperson, candidate for California State Assembly District 30, is honored to announce the endorsement of respected local business owner and community leader, Carina Powers. As a devoted advocate for community improvement, Carina's support highlights Dalila's dedication to addressing the critical needs of business owners and community members alike.
Carina Powers, a prominent business owner in Monterey County, shared her reasons for endorsing Dalila Epperson:
_“As a business owner, we are feeling the policies that are making it difficult to maintain our businesses. We need an individual who is truly engaged within the community to better understand our needs as business owners and as members of our communities,” stated Powers. She continued, “It is why I have carefully considered and officially endorsed Dalila Epperson as a candidate for California State Assembly for District 30. I have had the pleasure of knowing Dalila for several years now, as an activist; she has joined my communities from school board meetings standing strong for Parental Rights to the opening of our businesses during the shutdowns. I can confidently say that she possesses the necessary qualities and skills to excel in this position. Dalila Epperson is one such leader who has demonstrated her commitment to public service by volunteering for several causes, and I believe she will continue to work tirelessly to make our community a better place.”_
Dalila Epperson expressed her gratitude for Carina Powers' endorsement and support stating, "I am truly honored to receive Carina Powers' endorsement. Her dedication to our community and her insights as a local business owner are invaluable. I am committed to advocating for the needs of our business owners and ensuring that they receive the support they deserve. Together, we can create a thriving community where every individual and business can flourish."
Dalila Epperson’s campaign continues to gain momentum with strong community support and endorsements from influential local leaders like Carina Powers. Dalila remains focused on her mission to bring positive change to District 30 through dedicated public service and community engagement.
For more information about Dalila and her campaign, visit [www.dalilaforassembly.com.](https://hooverforassembly.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e0012af7e4c1c7f661725478e&id=e88425afec&e=4bbfb0c664)

# [#]
Happy Juneteenth.

On Juneteenth, we celebrate the emancipation of enslaved African Americans, reflect on the injustices that have historically been inflicted upon Black Americans, and acknowledge what still needs to be done to create an equitable nation for all.

It is important to never forget our nation’s history and remember that the fight for equal rights and opportunity for Black Americans remains ongoing. The systemic oppression, such as policies and laws that have historically kept racial minorities in poverty and disadvantaged, that Black Americans continue to face is an issue we must all work to overcome every single day. Together, we must learn from our nation’s history of violent oppression against people of color and continuously call out and push back against oppression, bias, and hate when we see it in our everyday lives.

Today and every day, I am committed to standing up against racial injustice and celebrating freedom. I hope you will join me today in celebration of the progress we have made so far and in acknowledgment of the work that still needs to be done.

Thank you,

Raul

| | |

Juneteenth holds profound significance for those of us dedicated to the cause of social justice, as it marks the day when the final enslaved African Americans in the United States were finally granted their freedom, two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation. **June 19th serves as a poignant reminder of the arduous journey towards racial equality and the ongoing fight for justice in our nation.** As we celebrate this important federal holiday, we must acknowledge the necessary work that remains to achieve genuine equality for everyone. We must elect leaders who will champion policies addressing systemic racism, economic disparities, and social injustices. It is imperative to dismantle the structures that perpetuate discrimination and ensure that every individual, regardless of race, gender, or background, has equal opportunities to thrive. **Let us recommit ourselves on this Juneteenth to the battle for equality and justice, and let us diligently work to elect leaders who will uphold these principles and establish a more fair and just society for all.** If you are not Black and unsure of how to support this holiday, consider taking action along with your words of celebration. Support Black-owned businesses, offer to cover a Black colleague's shift so they can participate in festivities, and dedicate time to educating yourself on the issues surrounding racial equality. clean_body: | | | Juneteenth holds profound significance for those of us dedicated to the cause of social justice, as it marks the day when the final enslaved African Americans in the United States were finally granted their freedom, two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation. June 19th serves as a poignant reminder of the arduous journey towards racial equality and the ongoing fight for justice in our nation. As we celebrate this important federal holiday, we must acknowledge the necessary work that remains to achieve genuine equality for everyone. We must elect leaders who will champion policies addressing systemic racism, economic disparities, and social injustices. It is imperative to dismantle the structures that perpetuate discrimination and ensure that every individual, regardless of race, gender, or background, has equal opportunities to thrive. Let us recommit ourselves on this Juneteenth to the battle for equality and justice, and let us diligently work to elect leaders who will uphold these principles and establish a more fair and just society for all. If you are not Black and unsure of how to support this holiday, consider taking action along with your words of celebration. Support Black-owned businesses, offer to cover a Black colleague's shift so they can participate in festivities, and dedicate time to educating yourself on the issues surrounding racial equality. In solidarity, Derek Marshall for Congress is a Democrat running for Congress in California's 23rd District. When I was on the Broward County Commission, I pushed the county to recognize this holiday so that we could reflect on this important part of our country's history. Though we've made crucial steps forward, the fight for equality continues. From improving healthcare access to fighting against climate change’s disproportionate impact on Black and Brown communities, there is still work to be done. As Congressman, you can count on me to help continue that work. Today and every day, let's continue to fight for equal opportunity and justice for all and honor the trailblazers who helped bring an end to slavery. Happy Juneteenth, \- Jared

Netanyahu is a war criminal overseeing the genocide and ethnic cleansing

subject: Celebrating Juneteenth
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Indiana Democratic Party, www
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP03/1/67635/images/IDP%20logo.jpg]
Peter,

We’re reaching out to wish you a very happy Juneteenth, a day of profound historical significance that ushered in a new era in America’s fight to attain racial equality.

[https://lh7-us.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeSs5U60MHCSBBcJo7NT34HKP-WCHXAaOqIbZkNXt2JIQCLDagH2XtfmRBFPp8GeXnAmlmEou6N06x8GV_OVAqMBFcst0aDm-Zr9BCsE0ldkA-WEdZJKB2YFQ_vWreivzdW_RaMfCvgK7Fbyg3HGJbHDoZp?key=HwG1_CwcNtu9-cJKUbetXQ]

Juneteenth commemorates the emancipation of the last enslaved African Americans in Galveston, Texas, on June 19, 1865. Today, we continue to celebrate it as a way to honor the resilience and beauty of America’s Black communities.

As Democrats, we embrace the values that Juneteenth represents: justice, inclusivity, equality, and equity. We know that this day serves not only as a cause for celebration, but also as a reminder of how far we have yet to go as a nation.

That’s why today and everyday, we renew our commitment to making Indiana a safer and kinder place to live, because it is only through unity that we will be able to build a brighter state for all Hoosiers.

Happy Juneteenth, everybody! We wish you well.

Thanks,
INDems

Indiana Democratic Party
101 W Washington St., #1110E
Indianapolis, IN 46204

name: Christopher & Brian Worrell
subject: The importance of Juneteenth
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Logo.png]
Dear Friends-
Today is Juneteenth -- a day that represents the end of slavery in the United States and serves as a powerful symbol of Black resilience and the ongoing struggle for equality.
On June 19, 1865, nearly two years after President Abraham Lincoln emancipated enslaved Black people, Union soldiers arrived in Galveston Bay, Texas, delivering the message of freedom and officially ending slavery in America. It honors this significant milestone in American history and encourages reflection on the nation's progress and the work still needed to achieve true racial justice.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Worrell%20Brothers%20Juneteenth%202.jpeg]
Juneteenth serves as a powerful reminder of the strength of those who came before us -- fighting for their rights and freedoms against a backdrop of immense adversity, racism, and violence. Celebrating Juneteenth fosters a deeper understanding and appreciation of Black history and culture, promoting a sense of unity and reflection on the progress made and the work still to be done in the pursuit of equality.
We hope you will join us in reflecting on this important day in American history, honoring the bravery and selflessness of countless Black Americans (both notable and unknown), and joining us in the fight for racial equity.
Sincerely,
State Representative Christopher Worrell
Boston City Councilor Brian Worrell

My opponent, Rep. Jack Bergman, and other Republicans want to reduce food assistance for millions of Americans by depleting SNAP benefits from the Farm Bill.
SNAP costs $6 per day for each American struggling with hunger. Meanwhile, Bergman charged taxpayers $79 per day for his own meal reimbursements, the highest among all members of Congress.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/92793/images/EBTs%20Farm.png]

➤ WHY THE FARM BILL MATTERS ➤ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mi1farming]
Friends,
Over the past three years, I have had the privilege of visiting numerous small farms in Northern Michigan and the UP. One thing is clear - Rural agriculture thrives when we invest in programs that prioritize sustainability and people.
Republicans and Democrats have introduced different proposals for the Farm Bill, and the GOP version is trying to make it harder for seniors, children, and people with disabilities to receive food assistance.
Rather than cutting these programs, the American people want Congress to focus on why so many Americans need supplemental nutrition assistance and address issues like low wages, inadequate childcare, and a lack of accessible healthcare.
Our mission is clear.
This is why the Farm Bill matters. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mi1farming]

1. **Abortion rights:** Republican legislators are rolling back abortion rights around the country. One of Senate Republicans' top priorities is to pass a _national abortion ban_.

clean_body: Donate now to split a donation between my campaign & EMILYs List >> | = = Peter, There are plenty of reasons why we need to do whatever it takes to defend our narrow Senate majority, but I'll do my best to narrow it down to five. = | = = Here are my top five reasons, Peter: 1. Abortion rights: Republican legislators are rolling back abortion rights around the country. One of Senate Republicans' top priorities is to pass a national abortion ban. 2. Climate crisis: We can't take chances when it comes to preserving our planet. Democrats passed the largest investment in green energy and jobs in our country's history, and Republicans are eager to repeal it. 3. Voting rights: When more people vote, Republicans lose. So the GOP wants to make it harder for people to vote by chipping away at the Voting Rights Act and passing voting restrictions. 4. Lowering costs: A Republican-controlled Senate would pass another massive tax cut for corporations and the ultra-wealthy, leaving working families to shoulder the burden. 5. The Supreme Court: We've already seen the far-right court overturn Roe v. Wade and overrule student debt relief. Democrats need Senate control to have a say in future nominations. For all these reasons (and so many more), we MUST defend our majority, Peter. In just a moment, we are going to ask you to make your first contribution to President Biden's reelection campaign. Please give us a chance to explain why this request -- especially right now -- is so important. Here's the truth: June is an FEC fundraising deadline month. This means that at the end of the month we will be required to report how much money we've raised and how many donations we've received. Everyone will be watching -- the press, our opponent, and even supporters will be waiting to see the strength of our campaign. We've received a huge number of individual donations so far -- people of all backgrounds and from all communities. It's a big part of how we've been able to withstand the millions and millions of dollars Republicans are spending on attack ads. But today, Joe Biden and Kamala Harris need you. Because this is the most important fundraising deadline of the presidential election yet. [Can President Biden count on you to contribute $5, $10, or whatever you can afford today? | Peter,

Today is Juneteenth, a day to commemorate the emancipation of enslaved people in the United States. On June 19th, 1865, more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was signed, enslaved Black Americans in Galveston, Texas, finally learned of their freedom.

Juneteenth stands as a powerful symbol of liberation, marking the end of a dark chapter in our history and the beginning of a new journey toward justice and equality.

This day is not only a celebration of freedom but also an opportunity to reflect on our past, recognize the progress we have made, and recommit to the work that still lies ahead. In recent times, we have witnessed renewed struggles for equality for all. Issues such as voting rights, police brutality, and systemic discrimination remind us that the fight for justice is ongoing.

I vow to continue to work with other lawmakers on comprehensive reforms to right these wrongs, and I am committed to supporting policies that promote equity to create a more inclusive and fair society for all.

**Official Voter Pamphlet Support Statement** As leaders of Alaskans for Honest Elections 22AKHE, We ask you to support this initiative to get rid of the Open Primary System and Ranked-Choice Voting (RCV) in Alaska. We think this change is important to make our elections easier, cheaper, and clearer. Why This Matters: 1\. High Costs: o Ranked-Choice Voting is very expensive. Since we started using it, our election costs have gone up to over $11 million, from about $3.3 million per year between 2010 and 2020. 2022 Election was 328% more expensive than every election from 2010-2020. o This money could be used for other important things in our state. 2\. Low Voter Turnout: o RCV has made voting confusing for many people. This confusion has led to the lowest voter turnout in Alaska’s history. o When voting is too complicated, people don’t vote. This is bad for our democracy. 3\. Misleading Results: o RCV doesn’t always show a clear winner. Sometimes, if a voter’s chosen candidate is eliminated early, their vote doesn’t count in the final result. o This means the winner might not be who most voters wanted. 4\. Hurts 3rd Parties: o RCV was supposed to help smaller, third-party candidates, but it hasn’t worked. In 2022, no third-party candidates made it to the U.S. Senate race. In 2020 ther were Five 3rd party candidates in the U.S. Senate race. o This shows that RCV isn’t giving us more choices as promised. 5\. Dirty Politics: o The Jungle Primary system, where all candidates run together regardless of party, has led to more negative campaigning within parties. o In 2022, even though Republican candidates got more overall votes, a Democrat won because of how RCV counted the votes. 6\. Too Many Candidates: o RCV has brought more candidates into elections, but this hasn’t improved the quality of choices. Instead, it makes elections more confusing and expensive. o For example, in the 2022 U.S. House election, 48 candidates ran, but only 4 made it to the general election. Over 90% of these candidates had no real chance to win. o A closed primary system, where parties choose their best candidate, is simpler and gives voters clearer choices. 7\. Impact on Minority Voters: o RCV often harms minority voters. Studies show that in places with lots of minority voters, ballots get “exhausted” more often. This means their votes don’t count in the final rounds. o Minority voters also tend to have less information about all the candidates, which makes it harder for them to rank many candidates, leading to their votes being wasted. Conclusion: Supporting this initiative will make our elections simpler and save money. It will make voting easier and ensure that more people’s voices are heard. Let’s bring back a clear and honest election system in Alaska. Please vote for 22AKHE. We believe this change is necessary for fairer and more effective elections in Alaska.

We think this change is important to make our elections easier, cheaper, and clearer. Why This Matters: 1\. High Costs: o Ranked-Choice Voting is very expensive. Since we started using it, our election costs have gone up to over $11 million, from about $3.3 million per year between 2010 and 2020. 2022 Election was 328% more expensive than every election from 2010-2020. o This money could be used for other important things in our state. 2\. Low Voter Turnout: o RCV has made voting confusing for many people. This confusion has led to the lowest voter turnout in Alaska’s history. o When voting is too complicated, people don’t vote. This is bad for our democracy. 3\. Misleading Results: o RCV doesn’t always show a clear winner. Sometimes, if a voter’s chosen candidate is eliminated early, their vote doesn’t count in the final result. o This means the winner might not be who most voters wanted. 4\. Hurts 3rd Parties: o RCV was supposed to help smaller, third-party candidates, but it hasn’t worked. In 2022, no third-party candidates made it to the U.S. Senate race. In 2020 ther were Five 3rd party candidates in the U.S. Senate race. o This shows that RCV isn’t giving us more choices as promised. 5\. Dirty Politics: o The Jungle Primary system, where all candidates run together regardless of party, has led to more negative campaigning within parties. o In 2022, even though Republican candidates got more overall votes, a Democrat won because of how RCV counted the votes. 6\. Too Many Candidates: o RCV has brought more candidates into elections, but this hasn’t improved the quality of choices. Instead, it makes elections more confusing and expensive. o For example, in the 2022 U.S. House election, 48 candidates ran, but only 4 made it to the general election. Over 90% of these candidates had no real chance to win. o A closed primary system, where parties choose their best candidate, is simpler and gives voters clearer choices. 7\. Impact on Minority Voters: o RCV often harms minority voters. Studies show that in places with lots of minority voters, ballots get “exhausted” more often. This means their votes don’t count in the final rounds. o Minority voters also tend to have less information about all the candidates, which makes it harder for them to rank many candidates, leading to their votes being wasted. Conclusion: Supporting this initiative will make our elections simpler and save money. It will make voting easier and ensure that more people’s voices are heard. Let’s bring back a clear and honest election system in Alaska. Please vote for 22AKHE. Friend, I am taking today as a day of celebration and reflection, both as a Black man and as Governor of Maryland. Juneteenth is marked as the second Independence Day of America. It was on this day in 1865 that Union troops arrived in Galveston, Texas with the news that the more than 250,000 enslaved Black people in the state were free. Though the Emancipation Proclamation brought this freedom on January 1st, 1863, it took **more than two years** for this freedom to be brought all the way out west to states such as Texas. **This is why Juneteenth exists.** It wasn’t until 2021 that Juneteenth was recognized as a federal holiday by President Biden. We still see acts of injustice against Black Americans to this day. Juneteenth is not only a time to celebrate, but a time to reflect. In that reflection, I ask you to challenge yourself: What do you see for the future of America and its freedoms? What does freedom mean to you? How can we achieve that freedom for all? | | | **Celebrating Juneteenth and Building a Stronger Community Together****!**
---

Dear Peter,
As we commemorate Juneteenth, we honor the enduring spirit of freedom and resilience in our great nation. This day marks a pivotal moment in American history, celebrating the emancipation of enslaved African Americans and reminding us of the ongoing journey toward equality and justice.
Our campaign in Washington's 8th Congressional District is committed to upholding the values of liberty, opportunity, and unity that Juneteenth represents. We believe in fostering a community where every individual can thrive, and your support is crucial to achieving this vision.
This Juneteenth, we ask for your help to continue our efforts in advocating for policies that promote economic growth, support small businesses, and ensure equal opportunities for all. Your donation will enable us to reach more voters, spread our message, and work towards a brighter future for our district.

---
| | | |
---
|
Whether you can give $10, $20, or any amount, your contribution will make a significant impact.
Together, we can celebrate the progress we’ve made and continue the work towards a more inclusive and prosperous community.

name: Dr. Cornel West
subject: West | Abdullah 2024 Celebrates Black Liberation
body:
On this Juneteenth, we must invest ourselves in the deep and long reparations struggle by honoring those who committed their life to this work. We call the names Belinda Sutton Royall, Sojourner Truth, Callie House and Isaiah Dickerson, Queen Mother Moore, Randall Robinson, John Conyers

| | |
---
---
---
#### Greetings, Loved Ones
Happy Juneteenth! On this day of Jubilee, we celebrate the unfinished job of Black freedom. We honor our courageous and visionary Ancestors, who brought us this far down freedom’s road. We cling to the community that has always served as our refuge. We pledge to our children and future generations the continued struggle to make us free, not simply “free-ish.” On June 19, 1865, General Gordon Granger delivered Field Order Number 3 to enslaved Black people in Galveston, Texas, two-and-a-half years after Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation. What should be made clear is that our divinely led, brave, visionary Ancestors immediately defied that Order, which instructed them to “remain quietly at their present homes and work for wages.” Our beloved grandmothers, grandfathers took the issuance of the Field Order as an opening to seek full Black freedom. They praised and honored the Creator - establishing churches and places of worship, developing intellectual tools through collective study, founding schools and colleges; they searched for loved ones who had been kidnapped and sold away from them, building Black towns and businesses, they honed creative tools and birthed art, and they demanded reparations to begin to repair the damage brought by centuries of attempted dehumanization, stolen labor, and stolen lives.
---
|
---
| Both Dr. West and I descend directly from this tradition. His people are from Orange, Texas, and mine are from Beaumont, right up the road from Galveston. **We owe our Ancestors the demand, struggle, and victory of reparations. This is why**[**reparations are central to our policy pillars **](https://www.cornelwest2024.com/platform?e=2c4ab4fbefc09c0d9c12f8df438b31c5&utm_source=cornelwest&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=professor_abdullah_juneteenth&n=1)**in our historic run for the Presidency of the United States.**
---
On this Juneteenth, we must invest ourselves in the deep and long reparations struggle by honoring those who committed their life to this work. We call the names Belinda Sutton Royall, Sojourner Truth, Callie House and Isaiah Dickerson, Queen Mother Moore, Randall Robinson, John Conyers, and countless others. We immerse ourselves in study and invest deeply in the contemporary struggle even as we take this day of celebration. For those who are not Black, we invite you to pledge solidarity with the understanding that reparations is a core moral, ethical, and legal principle that must be applied to the stolen labor and lives of African people. Support reparations and make financial contributions to Black-led organizations that are doing this vital work. Reparations is a debt that is owed to Black people and must be paid in order to stabilize the nation and advance together. Dr. West and I are committed to making reparations real. We are grateful to contemporary reparations activists and organizations and applaud locales and states that are building their own reparations policies as first steps. As Black people rightfully celebrate this day of Jubilee, we also commit to the continued work of Black freedom that only comes with reparations.
---
---
In Truth, Justice, and Love,
#### Melina Abdullah
_Great-great-great granddaughter of Rachel...a free African woman who was stolen, chained, bound, and imported as chattel into Sabine Pass, Texas_ And Independent Candidate for Vice President of the United States

| **Fresno Sheriff John Zanoni Endorses Congressman John Duarte**
---
| | **Fresno, CA** — Fresno County Sheriff John Zanoni is endorsing Congressman John Duarte for reelection. Sheriff Zanoni was born and raised in Fresno County, where he was elected as Sheriff in 2022 following a 26-year career keeping Valley families safe.

Sheriff Zanoni endorsed Congressman Duarte because of Duarte’s success in bringing Republicans and Democrats together to keep Valley families safe. _“John Duarte is someone we can count on to keep Valley families safe,”_ said Sheriff Zanoni._“He is working with local leaders from both parties to clean up our streets and get our hardworking law enforcement the support they need. I fully endorse Duarte’s campaign and look forward to continuing to work with him.”_

In response to the endorsement, John Duarte stated, _“Sheriff Zanoni stands for law and order, supports victims, and works tirelessly for a safer Fresno County. I am honored to earn the trust of a leader like him.”_

Sheriff Zanoni joins an impressive list of law enforcement leaders, organizations, and advocates from both political parties endorsing Duarte's campaign. Duarte is prioritizing the Valley’s safety in Washington. He introduced the HIDTA reauthorization bill to provide over $300 million to fight drugs like Fentanyl and meth. For more information about John Duarte and his campaign, please visit [www.JohnDuarteforCongress.com](https://johnduarteforcongress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d614871a572868b235b65477d&id=df8fb7a373&e=76a47b375f).

name: LCV Membership Team
subject: This Juneteenth, take action for Black communities harmed by pollution
body:
We must not reverse course on environmental justice.

| | | |
---
|
* * *
---
| | | | Peter — each year, Juneteenth brings a celebration of the resilience and independence of our country’s Black communities, while reminding us, in the eternal words of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., that "justice too long delayed is justice denied."
---
| | Although President Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in January 1863, it wasn’t until June 19th, 1865 that enslaved Black people in Galveston, Texas learned of their freedom. That is why our country now officially commemorates June 19th, or “Juneteenth,” as the day when the nation’s last enslaved people finally received word of their long overdue emancipation.
---
| | Despite all of the progress we’ve made since then, Black communities continue to be disproportionately harmed by climate change, polluted air and water, voter suppression, and exclusion from conservation and recreation opportunities. **And extreme lawmakers in Congress are working nonstop to defund, block, and overturn efforts to rectify these historic injustices.**
---
| | For example, on June 5, anti-environmental lawmakers in the House voted 209-197 to pass H.R. 8580, which would _block all funding_ for the Biden-Harris administration’s environmental justice agenda, known as Justice40 for its goal of directing at least 40% of federal clean energy and climate investments to communities that are overburdened by pollution.
---
| | This and other bills targeting environmental justice are headed to the Senate — **we need your help to make it clear that the environmental movement will not accept any legislation that delays, defunds, or blocks environmental justice from Black and other historically marginalized communities.**
---
| | [**_Please, take action today. Write to your elected officials and tell them to oppose any legislation that reverses course on environmental justice. It only takes a moment to make your voice heard >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/w_ywTd-_)
---
| | Under President Biden’s Justice40 commitment, at least 40% of federal investments in combating climate change, upgrading to clean energy infrastructure, and building sustainable housing are set to be directed to communities that have been disproportionately impacted by climate change and pollution, including Black communities.
---
| | Ever since the Biden administration announced this commitment, extreme MAGA lawmakers have vowed to overturn it and eliminate environmental justice funding altogether. **Their relentless attacks continue a racist legacy of delaying and denying justice of all kinds to Black communities, including protection from pollution, the freedom to vote, and equal economic opportunity.**
---
| | LCV is proud to fight for a healthier planet and a stronger democracy for all Americans — and we’re so grateful to have you in our movement. [**This Juneteenth, we hope you’ll join us in taking action: tell your lawmakers today that they must oppose any legislation that reverses course on environmental justice >>**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/YYbZBy9DZZT~)
---
| | Thank you, Peter. We’ll be in touch soon with more updates on our campaigns for people and our planet.
---
| | Onward,

body:
Trump's bizarre hour-long interview
| | |
---
In a surprise to no one, friend, Donald Trump attacked me in a bizarre hour-long interview with Dr. Phil.
Before I share what he said about me, I need to underscore this:

**Donald Trump poses a unique and dangerous threat to our democracy. We are at risk of seeing a convicted felon, who has no regard for the rule of law, elected as President of the United States — a position from which he could do unspeakable damage to our democracy here at home, and democracies around the world.**
**_[Help me defeat him once and for all. Chip in a split donation between Debbie Mucarsel-Powell and my campaign of $5 today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87211659/480414726/-1984759417?&amounts=5,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=jtk1383-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS8xMDc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDdjNjI1MTktNzUyZS1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=KvdLSMpiBRB0Kzq2xVgud9ySbfj2wrTnKln21hiyuFw=)_**
| | [Contribute](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87211660/480414727/-1984759417?&amounts=5,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=jtk1383-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS8xMDc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDdjNjI1MTktNzUyZS1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=KvdLSMpiBRB0Kzq2xVgud9ySbfj2wrTnKln21hiyuFw=)
---
In an hour-long softball interview with Dr. Phil, Trump attacked the judge in the New York trial, President Biden, and the jury of 12 Americans who unanimously ruled he was guilty of 34 felony counts. **He came after me as well.**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87211661/480414728/-1984759417?&amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1383-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS8xMDc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDdjNjI1MTktNzUyZS1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=KvdLSMpiBRB0Kzq2xVgud9ySbfj2wrTnKln21hiyuFw=)
_“**I call him watermelon head.** He’s got the thinnest neck I’ve ever seen. Very unattractive guy, both inside and outside. **These are bad people.** ”_
Friend, trust me — I’ve been called a lot worse by Donald Trump and his MAGA cronies.
**What concerns me far more is how Trump, in this very interview and numerous other recent campaign events, has explicitly called for revenge against his political rivals._Rivals like me. Like his call to prosecute me and other members of the January 6 Committee._**
God forbid Trump makes it back to the White House, he will use his powers to seek retribution against the people who have held him accountable for his crimes and disgraceful behavior. Including me.
He tried to do this during his first term, and he lashed out at his former attorney general for not going after rivals with baseless investigations and lawsuits. **But if he’s president for a second time, he’ll only appoint cabinet officials who do exactly what he wants.**

Donald Trump has promised to be a dictator on day one. He admires leaders like Vladimir Putin and Kim Jong Un. That’s the risk he poses to our country.
